definition_zh: 明显地；显而易见地；显然；不用说；当然
definition_en: in a way that is easy to see or understand; also used to present something as clear from the facts or from common sense
core_image: 一件东西横在路中央，谁走过来都绕不开，也一眼就看见
scene: 教室的灯一亮，黑板上的错字立刻露了出来，门口站着的人都能看见。 The mistake on the board was obviously a typo, and the teacher smiled.
sceneCN: 这里是「明显地、一眼可见」（第 1 个义项：以容易看见或理解的方式）；句意为黑板上的错误一看就是笔误，老师笑了笑。可辨物件：黑板、粉笔字、刚亮起的灯。

pos.zh: 明显地；显而易见地；显然；当然

derivatives.zh: obviously 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「明显的」
由 obvious 加 -ness 构成，义为「明显；显而易见」
与 obvious 同源于拉丁语 obviare，义为「消除；预先防止」

senses.title: In a way that is easy to see or understand
senses.definition: in a manner that is easy to notice, see or understand
senses.definitionCN: 以容易察觉、看见或理解的方式
senses.example: The road was obviously blocked by the fallen tree.
senses.exampleCN: 那条路明显被倒下的树堵住了。
senses.why: Obvious comes from Latin obvius, something standing in one's way, right in front of the eyes, so what is obviously true needs no searching.
senses.whyCN: obvious 源自拉丁语 obvius，指挡在眼前、迎面而来的东西；所以 obviously 描述的是不用寻找、抬眼就看得见的事。

senses.title: Used to state what any listener should accept
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to present something as clear from the facts or from common sense
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句开头，把某事说成从事实或常识看来很清楚的
senses.example: Obviously, a plan that costs nothing cannot build a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 显然，一个不花钱的方案是造不成桥的。
senses.why: Once a fact is placed right before the eyes, the speaker can invite the listener to see it too, which is how the word becomes a sentence opener.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事实被摆到眼前，说话人就可以请听话人一起「看见」它，这个词于是成了句子开头的引子。

senses.title: Used in speech to underline or agree
senses.definition: used in conversation to stress a point or to agree that something is plain
senses.definitionCN: 在会话中强调某一点，或表示某事明摆着、无需多说
senses.example: Obviously you must call before you visit.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，你来之前得先打个电话。
senses.why: In quick conversation the literal picture fades and the word becomes a nudge, telling the listener that the point is too plain to miss.
senses.whyCN: 在快速的口语里，字面的画面淡去了，这个词变成一个小小的提醒：告诉对方这一点太明显，不会漏掉。

intro.en: Obviously is the adjective obvious wearing the adverb suffix -ly, and obvious began as a picture of something placed directly in a road.
intro.cn: obviously 是形容词 obvious 加上副词后缀 -ly 构成的，而 obvious 最初画的是一件横在路中央的东西。

items.en: Via meant way or road, and it survives in English in phrases such as by way of.
items.cn: via 意为道路、路线，在英语里还留在表示「经由」的说法中。

items.en: Ob- plus via made obvius, literally in the way, and therefore standing before the eyes and plain to see.
items.cn: ob- 与 via 合成 obvius，字面是「在路上」，因此引申为「在眼前、一眼可见」。

items.en: English borrowed obvious for what lies in the way, is exposed to view and needs no explaining.
items.cn: 英语借入 obvious，指挡在路上、暴露在视线里、无需解释的东西。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the adjective settled into its modern sense of easy to see or understand.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个形容词固定为现代义：容易看见或容易理解。

items.en: Adding -ly created the adverb, whose sentence-initial use for it is clear that became common in modern writing and speech.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 造出副词，其中放在句首表示「显然、可以想见」的用法，在现代书面语与口语里都变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin words for road and for facing; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of clarity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「道路」与「迎面」之上的同族词，近义组收其他表示清楚的副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a road with something lying across it: obvius means in the way, and -ly turns that picture into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条路，路上横着东西：obvius 意为「挡在路上」，-ly 把这幅画面变成副词。

normal.en: Obvious comes from obvius, something that stands in the way, right before the eyes.
normal.cn: obvious 源自 obvius，指挡在路上、就在眼前的东西。

normal.en: Via is the Latin word for road, and obvius is what lies in the road ahead of you.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语里的「道路」，obvius 就是横在你前头路上的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective obvious into the adverb obviously without adding a new meaning.
normal.cn: -ly 只是把形容词 obvious 变成副词 obviously，并不增添新的意思。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence, obviously tells the listener that the facts are already visible.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，obviously 等于告诉听话人：事实已经摆在那里了。

normal.en: In speech, obviously sometimes just means of course and carries a hint of impatience.
normal.cn: 在口语里，obviously 有时就是「当然」，还带着一点不耐烦的意味。

abstract.en: An object placed in the middle of a road needs no sign to be noticed.
abstract.cn: 一件横在路中央的东西，不需要竖牌子也会被注意到。

abstract.en: What is obvious is often obvious only after someone has pointed at it.
abstract.cn: 所谓明显，往往要有人指出之后才显得明显。

abstract.en: Repeating obviously too often makes the speaker sound as if the listener is slow.
abstract.cn: 把 obviously 说得太频繁，会让说话人显得把听者当成反应慢的人。

examples.en: The mistake on the board was obviously a typo, and the teacher smiled.
examples.cn: 黑板上的错误一看就是笔误，老师笑了笑。

examples.en: Obviously, a plan that costs nothing cannot build a bridge.
examples.cn: 显然，一个不花钱的方案是造不成桥的。

examples.en: Obviously you must call before you visit.
examples.cn: 当然，你来之前得先打个电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥伯维死理」——明摆着的事像死理一样不用争；记住 obviously 是显然。

root: 拉丁语 via（道路）→ obvius（挡在路上的、迎面可见的）→ 英语 obvious（明显的）+ 后缀 -ly → obviously（明显地）；同族词多与「路、迎面」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something lying in plain view; the senses divide into the manner sense, the sentence-opening assertion, and the spoken emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「摆在眼前、看得见」；义项分成方式副词、句首断言，以及口语里的强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single object lying across a road, impossible to walk around and impossible to miss.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西横在路中央，绕不过去，也躲不开视线。

branches.cn: 白板上一眼就看见的错字

branches.en: a road stopped by a tree in plain view
branches.cn: 路上横着一棵明摆着的树

branches.en: a fact spread out on the table for all to see

intro.cn: 这个词立在表示道路的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词，以及一个把形容词变成副词的英语后缀之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin via and the adjective obvius supply the whole family, and obviam, the phrase for in the way, explains the picture inside the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 via 与形容词 obvius 支撑整族词，而表示「迎面、挡在路上」的短语 obviam 解释了词里藏着的画面。

definition_zh: 吸引；引起（注意、兴趣）；招致（批评、麻烦）
definition_en: to pull someone or something toward a place, or to make people interested or notice something
core_image: 一块磁石把四周的铁屑都拉成一个小圈
scene: 夜市摊主把灯调亮，路过的人不由自主地靠近。 The bright stall attracted a crowd within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 attract 是「吸引」（第 1 个义项：把人或物拉向自己）；句意是明亮的摊位几分钟内就吸引了一群人。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有吸引力的；好看的

senses.title: Draw near
senses.definition: to pull someone or something toward a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物拉向某处或某人
senses.example: The flowers attract bees in early summer.
senses.exampleCN: 初夏时这些花吸引蜜蜂。
senses.why: The Latin base trahere means 'to draw or pull', so the first sense is a physical pull, as a magnet draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 trahere 意为「拉、拖」，所以第一义项是物理意义上的拉近，像磁石把铁吸过来。

senses.title: Arouse interest
senses.definition: to make people interested in something or make them notice it
senses.definitionCN: 使人对某事物产生兴趣或注意到它
senses.example: The title attracted my attention at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标题立刻引起了我的注意。
senses.why: The pull moves from the body to the mind: eyes and curiosity are drawn toward the thing, though nothing physically moves.
senses.whyCN: 这种「拉」从身体转到心里：目光和好奇心被牵过去，物体本身并没有移动。

senses.title: Bring something bad
senses.definition: to cause something unpleasant to come to you
senses.definitionCN: 招来不愉快的事，如批评或麻烦
senses.example: His remarks attracted sharp criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言论招致尖锐的批评。
senses.why: Here the pull works in reverse: your own words or deeds draw consequences onto you, and those consequences are usually unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「拉」方向相反：自己的言行把后果拉到自己身上，而这类后果通常不受欢迎。

intro.en: Attract is built from a Latin verb meaning to draw something toward oneself.
intro.cn: attract 由拉丁语中表示「把东西拉向自己」的动词构成。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw, pull or drag'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、牵引」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus trahere made attrahere, 'to draw to oneself'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 trahere 构成 attrahere，意为「拉向自己」。

items.en: The past participle attractus described something already drawn near.
items.cn: 过去分词 attractus 描述已被拉近的东西。

items.en: English attracten first meant to draw or allure.
items.cn: 中古英语 attracten 最初表示拉近或引诱。

items.en: The word widened to interest, appeal and unwanted consequences.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到引起兴趣、产生吸引力以及招致不良后果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root tract; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of drawing people in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 tract；近义组是其他表示「把人拉过来」的动词。

normal.en: Picture a magnet: whatever it draws is attracted.

normal.en: Attract attention and attract interest are the two everyday patterns.

normal.en: Attract criticism shows the same pull applied to bad results.

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the adjective is attractive.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，形容词是 attractive。

abstract.cn: 想象铁屑跳起来，紧紧贴在磁石上。

abstract.en: See moths circling a bright window at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里飞蛾绕着一扇亮着的窗打转。

abstract.en: See a spotlight swing across a stage and stop on one singer.

examples.en: Bright colours attract young children.

definition_zh: 祝福；保佑；使有幸拥有
definition_en: to ask God to protect and help someone
core_image: 教堂里伸出的祝福之手
scene: 教堂门口，老人把手轻轻放在孩子头顶。 The priest blessed the couple at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 bless 是「祝福」（第 1 个义项：祈求神明护佑）；句意是牧师在门口为这对夫妇祝福。

pos.zh: 动词：使有幸拥有，赐予好事

derivatives.zh: 祝福；幸事，令人感激的好事

senses.title: To ask for divine protection
senses.definition: to ask God to protect and help a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 祈求神明保护并帮助某人或某物
senses.example: The priest blessed the couple at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师在门口为这对夫妇祝福。
senses.why: This is the central religious sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的宗教义项。

senses.title: To give someone a good thing
senses.definition: to give a person a valuable quality or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某人宝贵的品质或优势
senses.example: She is blessed with a fine voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她有幸拥有一副好嗓子。
senses.why: A gift from God became any fortunate gift.
senses.whyCN: 来自神明的赐予，扩展为任何幸运的馈赠。

senses.title: To give thanks over food
senses.definition: to ask God's blessing on a meal before eating
senses.definitionCN: 进食前祈求神明赐福这顿饭
senses.example: He blessed the food before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前他为食物做了祷告。
senses.why: The same prayer moved from people to the table.
senses.whyCN: 同样的祷告从人身上移到了餐桌上。

intro.en: Gasoline combines the short word gas with chemical endings for oil and for liquids.
intro.cn: gasoline 把短词 gas 与表示油和液体的化学词尾结合起来。

items.en: Khaos described empty space and gave rise to gas.
items.cn: khaos 描述虚空，是 gas 的来源。

items.en: Van Helmont coined gas from that Greek word.
items.cn: 范海尔蒙特根据那个希腊词创造了 gas。

items.en: Oleum meant oil and gave the ending -ol.
items.cn: oleum 意为油，提供了词尾 -ol。

items.en: Gasoline was coined for a light fuel from petroleum.
items.cn: gasoline 被创造出来，指来自石油的轻质燃料。

items.en: The word became the American name for motor fuel.
items.cn: 这个词成为美式英语中汽车燃料的名称。

note.en: Gasoline is compared with look-alike words and other names for fuel.
note.cn: 把 gasoline 与形近词以及其他燃料名称作比较。

entries.definition: an older spelling of gasoline
a thick sweet liquid used in medicine and food
a soft oily substance used on the skin
the British word for motor fuel
material burned to produce power
a heavier fuel used in some engines

normalIntro.en: Gasoline is the liquid that carries a car from one town to the next.
normalIntro.cn: gasoline 是把汽车从一个镇带到下一个镇的液体。

normal.en: The car needs gasoline before the trip.
normal.cn: 出发前汽车需要加汽油。

normal.en: Gasoline prices rose again this week.
normal.cn: 这周汽油价格又涨了。

normal.en: The gasoline engine starts quickly in cold weather.
normal.cn: 汽油发动机在冷天启动很快。

normal.en: The mechanic used gasoline to clean the parts.
normal.cn: 机修工用汽油清洗零件。

normal.en: They filled a tank of gasoline for the long drive.
normal.cn: 他们为长途驾驶加满了一箱汽油。

abstract.en: Gasoline turns ancient sunlight into present motion.
abstract.cn: 汽油把远古的阳光变成此刻的运动。

abstract.en: A full tank is a small kind of freedom.
abstract.cn: 满箱油是一种小小的自由。

abstract.en: We burn the past to reach the next place.
abstract.cn: 我们燃烧过去，以到达下一个地方。

sensesIntro.en: Gasoline is motor fuel refined from petroleum, or a light liquid used as a solvent.
sensesIntro.cn: gasoline 指从石油提炼的汽车燃料，或用作溶剂的轻质液体。

core.en: Refined oil that makes an engine move.
core.cn: 让发动机运转的提炼油品。

branches.en: A tank is filled before a journey.
branches.cn: 出发前油箱被加满。

branches.en: A workshop uses the liquid to clean parts.
branches.cn: 车间用这种液体清洗零件。

branches.en: An engine turns the fuel into motion.
branches.cn: 发动机把燃料变成运动。

branches.en: Fuel and solvent are the same refined liquid.
branches.cn: 燃料和溶剂是同一种提炼液体。

branches.en: The word marks the American name for petrol.
branches.cn: 这个词标志着美式英语对汽油的叫法。

intro.en: Gasoline builds words for engines, stations, and fuel blends.
intro.cn: gasoline 构成表示发动机、加油站和混合燃料的词。

latinIntro.en: The ending -ol comes from Latin oleum, meaning oil.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -ol 来自拉丁语 oleum，意为油。

The station sells gasohol in summer.

items.example: The gasoline engine is small and light.
items.exampleCN: 这台汽油发动机又小又轻。

Leaded gasoline is now banned in many places.

汽油价格一夜之间下降了。

definition_zh: 据推测；大概；想必
definition_en: as may reasonably be supposed from the available evidence
core_image: 桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚回来
scene: 实验室的门锁着，灯却亮着，同事据此推断有人来过。 The lights are on, so someone is presumably still inside.
sceneCN: 这里指根据迹象作出的合理推测（第 1 个义项：据推测）；句意为灯还亮着，所以想必里面还有人；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: As one may reasonably suppose
senses.definition: used to state what may reasonably be believed from the available evidence
senses.definitionCN: 说明根据现有证据可以合理相信的内容
senses.example: Presumably, the train was delayed by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 据推测，火车是被暴风雨耽误了。
senses.why: The adverb presents an inference, not a fact: the speaker expects the listener to accept the reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词呈现的是推断而非事实：说话者期待听者接受这套推理。

senses.title: Probably, but unconfirmed
senses.definition: used of a likely fact that has not been checked
senses.definitionCN: 指很可能成立却尚未核实的事实
senses.example: The keys are presumably in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙想必在抽屉里。
senses.why: The word marks probability resting on a normal expectation rather than on proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是建立在通常预期上的可能性，而不是证据。

senses.title: Sentence-opening inference
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, presenting a conclusion drawn from what precedes
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，呈现由前文推出的结论
senses.example: Presumably, the author meant a different example.
senses.exampleCN: 想必作者想说的是另一个例子。
senses.why: The initial position frames the whole clause as a reader's inference, common in commentary.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个小句框成读者的推断，这在评注文字中很常见。

senses.title: Presumably because
senses.definition: used to offer a likely explanation for something
senses.definitionCN: 用来为某事提出一个很可能的解释
senses.example: Presumably because of the rain, the match was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 想必是因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
senses.why: The pattern assigns a probable cause without claiming direct knowledge of it.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式给出可能的成因，却不声称直接知道它。

senses.title: Presumably not
senses.definition: used with not to state a likely negative conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，说出一个很可能的否定结论
senses.example: Presumably not everyone agreed with the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 想必并非人人都同意这个决定。
senses.why: Negation keeps the hedging: the speaker infers a negative rather than asserting it.
senses.whyCN: 否定保留了缓冲：说话者是在推断一个否定，而不是断言。

senses.title: Hedging in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的推测语气
senses.definition: in scholarship, a courteous way to attribute an unstated intention to an author
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，礼貌地把未明说的意图归给作者
senses.example: The passage is presumably an allusion to an older text.
senses.exampleCN: 这段文字想必是在暗指一部更早的文本。
senses.why: The hedge protects the writer from overclaiming about another person's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这一缓冲保护作者，免得对他人的意思说得过满。

senses.title: Legal presumption
senses.definition: in law, describing a fact treated as true unless it is rebutted
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，指除非被反驳否则视为真实的事实
senses.example: A person is presumably innocent until the case is proved.
senses.exampleCN: 在案件被证实之前，一个人被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the adverb into a rule about the burden of proof, not a casual guess.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个副词变成关于举证责任的规则，而不是随口猜测。

senses.title: Ironic dismissal
senses.definition: in speech, used ironically to suggest that something is only supposedly true
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中反讽地表示某事只是「据说」成立
senses.example: Presumably, that explanation satisfies everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 想必这个解释能让所有人满意吧。
senses.why: The ironic tone leans on the word's hedging: the speaker repeats a claim while doubting it.
senses.whyCN: 反讽语气借用了这个词的缓冲：说话者重复一个说法，同时表示怀疑。

intro.en: Presumably comes from the Latin verb for taking beforehand, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「预先拿取」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb sumere means to take or take up.
items.cn: 动词意为「拿、取」。

items.en: The prefix prae- means before or in advance.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前、预先」。

items.en: Praesumere means to take in advance, hence to assume or anticipate.
items.cn: 合成动词意为「预先拿走」，引申为「假定、预料」。

items.en: The noun praesumptio names an assumption taken beforehand.
items.cn: 名词指事先采取的假定。

items.en: English presume and presumable come through French and law; the adverb adds the usual suffix.
items.cn: 英语经法语与法学传统借入「假定」及其形容词，副词再加常见后缀。

items.en: Modern prose uses the adverb as a polite hedge in inference and academic commentary; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 现代散文用它作推断与学术评论中的礼貌缓冲；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin take-beforehand family, including a word with a stronger negative sense; the second group contrasts inference from evidence with plain probability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「预先拿取」词族，其中包括一个贬义更强的词；第二组对照「由证据推断」与「单纯的可能性」。

entries.definition: To suppose something to be true before proof; also to dare without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 在证据前就假定为真；也指未经许可擅自。

entries.definition: An assumption taken as true, or behaviour that goes too far.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为真的假定，或越界的行为。

entries.definition: Able to be supposed; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 可以推定的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: Going beyond what one has the right to do; the negative branch of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 越出本分、冒昧的；词族的贬义分支。

entries.definition: In all likelihood, without necessarily resting on a stated chain of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能，但不一定建立在明说的证据链上。

entries.definition: A formal phrase meaning very probably.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「很可能」的正式短语。

entries.definition: According to the normal course of things.
Certainly or very probably; a stronger and older word.
entries.definitionCN: 确实或很可能；更强、更旧的词。

entries.definition: As it appears from what is seen or reported, without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见或所闻看来如此，但未经证实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real take-beforehand root and the real difference between inference and plain probability.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「预先拿取」词根，并区分「推断」与「单纯可能」。

normal.en: The root means to take beforehand, so the speaker takes a conclusion before the proof arrives.
normal.cn: 词根意为「预先拿取」，所以说话者在证据到之前先把结论拿来。

normal.en: The lights are on, so someone is presumably inside: evidence first, conclusion second.
normal.cn: 灯亮着，所以想必有人在里面：先有迹象，再有结论。

normal.en: Presumably because does the same work as probably because, but sounds more careful.
normal.cn: 「想必是因为」与「很可能是因为」作用相同，但听起来更谨慎。

normal.en: In academic prose it lets a writer guess at an author's intention without claiming to know it.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它让作者猜测原作者意图，却不声称知道。

normal.en: In law, presumably innocent is a rule about who must prove what.
normal.cn: 在法律里，「推定无罪」是一条关于谁来举证的规定。

abstract.en: To presume is to lend a fact before it has earned trust.
abstract.cn: 推测就是在一件事尚未赢得信任之前先借给它。

abstract.en: The hedge keeps the door open in case the inference turns out wrong.
abstract.cn: 缓冲把门留着，以防推断最后错了。

abstract.en: Irony here works by repeating a claim with the doubt left showing at the edges.
abstract.cn: 这里的反讽靠重复一个说法，却让怀疑留在边缘。

examples.en: Presumably, the meeting was moved because of the holiday.
examples.cn: 想必会议是因为假日而改期。

examples.en: The document is presumably a copy, not the original.
examples.cn: 这份文件想必是副本，而不是原件。

examples.en: Presumably not all the guests were invited.
examples.cn: 想必并非所有客人都受到了邀请。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普瑞祖母布里」——祖母凭经验猜，大概如此

root: 拉丁语动词「拿取」加表示「预先」的前缀，构成「预先拿走、假定」，其名词指事先采取的假定；英语经法语与法学传统借入动词与形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate evidence-based inference, unconfirmed probability, sentence-opening inference, likely explanation, negated inference, academic hedging, legal presumption and ironic doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理据证推断、未证实的可能、句首推断、可能解释、否定推断、学术缓冲、法律推定，以及反讽怀疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping umbrella on the table while its owner is missing, so the reader guesses he just came in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚进来。

branches.en: THE INFERENCE: evidence leads to a conclusion, whether inside the sentence or at its head.
branches.cn: 推断：证据引出结论，无论在句中还是句首。

branches.en: THE UNCHECKED FACT: likely by normal expectation, not proved.
branches.cn: 未核事实：按通常预期很可能，却未获证明。

branches.en: THE LIKELY CAUSE: a probable explanation offered without direct knowledge.
branches.cn: 可能成因：在没有直接知识时给出的合理解释。

branches.en: THE HEDGE: negated inference and the courteous academic buffer.
branches.cn: 缓冲：否定式推断与学术上的礼貌缓冲。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE IRONY: legal burden of proof and the sceptical repeat.
branches.cn: 规则与反讽：法律举证责任与带怀疑的重复。

intro.en: Presumably is a Latin before-prefix, a taking-root, a noun of assumption, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「预先」前缀、「拿取」词根、表「假定」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is taking; the prefix puts the taking before the fact, which is exactly what an assumption does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是「拿取」；前缀把拿取放在事实之前，这正是「假定」所做的事。

items.example: The prefix puts the action ahead of the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放在证据之前。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical act of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「拿取」的具体动作。

items.example: The compound verb turns taking early into assuming.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「提前拿」变成「假定」。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun of assumption.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「假定」的名词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the English legal term.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语法律术语的基词。

items.example: English keeps both the thinking and the daring senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「思考」与「大胆」两条义。

items.example: The noun carries the same double life.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也带着同样的双重身份。

items.example: A different suffix pulls out the negative branch.
items.exampleCN: 另一个后缀拉出贬义分支。

items.example: The suffix turns presumable into a hedge adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成缓冲副词。

definition_zh: 存在；生存；靠…生活
definition_en: to be real or present; to live, especially in difficult conditions; to survive on something
core_image: 一样东西真实地立在那里并持续下去
scene: 问题在于这种鸟是否真的还存在。 The question is whether this bird still exists at all.
sceneCN: 这里 exist 是「存在」（第 1 个义项）；句意：问题在于这种鸟是否真的还存在。

derivatives.zh: 存在主义的；关于存在的

senses.title: Be real
senses.definition: to be real or present in the world
senses.definitionCN: 真实地存在于世界上
senses.example: Doubt still exists about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对这个计划仍有疑虑。
senses.why: The core sense is simply being there.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是真实地「在那里」。

senses.title: Stay alive
senses.definition: to live, especially in hard conditions
senses.definitionCN: 生存，尤指在艰苦环境中活着
senses.example: These animals exist in the deepest caves.
senses.exampleCN: 这些动物生存在最深的洞穴里。
senses.why: Being present is narrowed to being alive.
senses.whyCN: 「存在」收窄为「活着」。

senses.title: Live on
senses.definition: to manage to live with very little of something
senses.definitionCN: 靠很少的东西勉强维持生活
senses.example: The family existed on rice and beans for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人靠米饭和豆子熬过了一个月。
senses.why: Survival is tied to a small source of support.
senses.whyCN: 生存被具体化为依赖微薄的来源。

intro.en: Exist comes from Latin exsistere, to come forth or appear.
intro.cn: exist 源自拉丁语 exsistere，意为「出现、显现」。

items.en: Exsistere joins ex- (out) with sistere (to stand).
items.cn: exsistere 由 ex-（向外）与 sistere（站立）构成。

items.en: Exsistere means to step out and appear.
items.cn: exsistere 意为迈出并显现。

items.en: Exister carries the sense of being present.
items.cn: exister 带有「在场、存在」的含义。

items.en: Existen names the state of being.
items.cn: existen 指存在的状态。

items.en: Exist covers both being real and staying alive.
items.cn: exist 同时涵盖真实存在与活着。

items.en: Exist on adds the sense of surviving with little.
items.cn: exist on 增加了「靠很少东西生存」之意。

note.en: Exist means to be real; exit is a way out.
note.cn: exist 表示真实存在，exit 则是出口。

entries.definition: a way out of a place
to feel great joy
to use power or effort
to have reality or presence
to be alive
to happen or be found

normalIntro.en: Exist is about being real or staying alive.
normalIntro.cn: exist 讲的是真实存在或活下去。

normal.en: Life may exist under the ice of that moon.
normal.cn: 那颗卫星的冰层下也许存在生命。

normal.en: The old custom still exists in the village.
normal.cn: 这个古老习俗在村里依然存在。

normal.en: Some fish exist in total darkness.
normal.cn: 有些鱼生存在完全黑暗之中。

normal.en: The family existed on very little money.
normal.cn: 这家人靠很少的钱维持生活。

normal.en: Few of these trees exist outside the valley.
normal.cn: 这些树很少生长在山谷之外。

abstract.en: Picture a small light still burning in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中仍有一盏小灯亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine a shape that slowly comes into view.
abstract.cn: 想象一个轮廓慢慢浮现出来。

abstract.en: Think of a candle that refuses to go out.
abstract.cn: 想象一支怎么也不肯熄灭的蜡烛。

examples.en: Scientists wonder whether life exists on that planet.
examples.cn: 科学家想知道那颗行星上是否存在生命。

examples.en: The problem exists mainly in crowded cities.
examples.cn: 这个问题主要存在于拥挤的城市里。

examples.en: They existed for years on a tiny income.
examples.cn: 他们靠微薄的收入生活了很多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exist」读起来像「一个记斯特」，可以联想：只要被记住，就说明它真实「存在」过。

root: 拉丁语 exsistere（出现、存在）由 ex-（向外）与 sistere（站立）构成，核心义「站出来、显现而存在」。

sensesIntro.en: Exist means to be real, to stay alive, or to survive on a small amount.
sensesIntro.cn: exist 意为真实存在、活着，或靠很少的东西维持生存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something standing there as real.
core.cn: 核心意象：某样东西真实地立在那里。

branches.en: The basic sense is simply being real.
branches.cn: 基本义就是真实存在。

branches.en: Being real narrows to being alive.
branches.cn: 存在收窄为活着。

branches.en: Staying alive depends on a small source.
branches.cn: 活下去要依赖微薄的来源。

branches.en: Both describe something present in the world.
branches.cn: 两者都描述世界上在场的东西。

branches.en: Survival and living on are close in use.
branches.cn: 生存与靠某物活着用法相近。

intro.cn: exist 含有拉丁前缀 ex- 与动词 sistere。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exsistere 由 ex-（向外）与 sistere（站立）组合而成。

items.example: Sistere gives the root of standing.
Exsistere is the direct source of exist.
items.exampleCN: exsistere 是 exist 的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: exist 保留了拉丁语「显现」之义。

Existence names the state of being real.

Exsistere is the source of exist.

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；实际上；在实践中；以实用的方式；从实际出发
definition_en: almost or very nearly, in real conditions rather than in theory, or in a way that deals with real needs
core_image: 一只杯子立在桌边，水面几乎碰到杯口，只差一线就溢出
scene: 暴雨后的巷子里，积水已经漫到台阶最上一级。 By evening the road was practically a river.
sceneCN: 这里 practically 是「几乎、差不多」（第 1 个义项：非常接近但还不是）；句意为到了傍晚，这条路几乎成了一条河。图中可辨识物件：巷子、积水、台阶。

pos.zh: 几乎；差不多；实际上；在实践中；以实用的方式

derivatives.zh: 由 practically 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「实际的；实用的」
由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」
由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的；不可行的」

senses.title: Almost, very nearly
senses.definition: almost, so close to something that the difference hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 几乎，接近到差别几乎无关紧要的程度
senses.example: It is practically impossible to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚要写完这份报告几乎不可能。
senses.why: The sense grows out of the older meaning in effect: if something is true for every practical purpose, speakers slide from in effect to almost.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从较早的「在效果上」长出来：若一件事在所有实际用途上都成立，说话人便从「在效果上」滑到「几乎」。

senses.title: In real conditions rather than in theory
senses.definition: when real conditions are considered rather than the theory behind them
senses.definitionCN: 考虑真实条件，而不是背后的理论
senses.example: Practically speaking, the plan costs more than we can afford.
senses.exampleCN: 实际上，这个计划的费用超出我们的承受能力。
senses.why: The adverb is simply practical plus -ly, so it names the way things stand once an idea meets a real budget or a real room.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词就是 practical 加 -ly，指的就是一个想法碰上真实预算或真实房间之后的情形。

senses.title: In a practical way
senses.titleCN: 以实用的方式；从实际出发
senses.definition: by dealing with real things and real limits instead of following an abstract method
senses.definitionCN: 按真实的事物与限制来办事，而不照着抽象的方法做
senses.example: She fixed the pump practically, with a torch and a short list of steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手电筒和几行步骤，按实际可行的办法修好了水泵。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the plain -ly adverb of practical describes the manner of action, before the word ever came to mean almost.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：practical 加 -ly 的副词本义描述做事的方式，早于它表示「几乎」。

senses.title: Almost entirely, for all purposes
senses.definition: so nearly the case that for every practical purpose it is the case
senses.definitionCN: 接近到就一切实际用途而言即已成立
senses.example: The old mill is practically a ruin now.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊如今简直成了废墟。
senses.why: The legal phrase for all practical purposes was shortened into the adverb, and almost carries its force.
senses.whyCN: 法律短语 for all practical purposes 被压缩进这个副词，almost 承接了它的分量。

senses.title: In the real world, as opposed to books
senses.definition: with regard to what works in real life rather than in theory
senses.definitionCN: 就现实可行的一面而言，而非理论层面
senses.example: Practically, the engine needs a new pump.
senses.exampleCN: 从实际操作上说，这台发动机得换个泵。
senses.why: The adverb marks the move from theory to the workbench, which is its oldest employment.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记着从理论转到工作台的移动，这正是它最早的用法。

senses.title: Skillfully by hand
senses.definition: in a way that shows manual skill and good sense with things
senses.definitionCN: 以显示手上功夫和处事分寸的方式
senses.example: He repaired the fence practically, with bits of wire.
senses.exampleCN: 他用几段铁丝麻利地修好了篱笆。
senses.why: The manner sense of practical, being handy with real things, gives the adverb this workroom meaning.
senses.whyCN: practical「善于对付实物」的方式义，给了这个副词这种工坊里的含义。

senses.title: To all intents; as good as done
senses.definition: so close to completion that it may be treated as done
senses.definitionCN: 接近完成到可以当作已完成来对待
senses.example: With the roof on, the house is practically finished.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶装好，房子就算差不多完工了。
senses.why: Where the difference stops mattering, the practical mind crosses it out, and the adverb records that crossing.
senses.whyCN: 差别不再要紧之处，务实的目光就把它划掉，副词记下的正是这一笔。

senses.title: Used to soften a strong statement
senses.definition: used to make a strong claim less absolute, as a hedge
senses.definitionCN: 作为缓冲语，让强硬的说法不那么绝对
senses.example: It is practically certain that the train will be on time.
senses.exampleCN: 火车准点几乎是肯定的。
senses.why: Because it names the practical view rather than the absolute truth, the adverb lends its vagueness to bold claims.
senses.whyCN: 因为它指务实之见而非绝对真理，这个副词便把它的模糊性借给了大胆的断言。

intro.en: Practically is practical plus -ly, and both go back to a Greek verb for doing; the everyday sense almost is a later extension of in effect.
intro.cn: practically 是 practical 加 -ly，两者都上溯一个表示「做」的希腊动词；日常的「几乎」义是「在效果上」的后来引申。

items.en: The Greek verb prassein meant to do or to act, and praxis was the noun for action.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做、行动，名词 praxis 指行动。

items.en: Praktikos meant fit for action and described what serves doing rather than theorising.
items.cn: praktikos 意为适合行动的，用来形容服务于做而非空谈的东西。

items.en: Latin adopted the adjective as practicus, and its adverb practice carried the same sense of action.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 practicus，相应的副词同样带着「行动」的含义。

items.en: English formed practical from practice with -al, then added -ly to make the adverb in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语在 practice 上加 -al 造出 practical，十六、十七世纪又加 -ly 造出副词。

items.en: Modern English extended the adverb to mean almost, and phrases such as practically speaking keep both the old and the new senses in view.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词扩展到「几乎」，而 practically speaking 一类说法同时保留了旧义与新义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same practice family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of near-completeness and effect.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 practice 词族的形式；近义组收表示接近完成与效果实际的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning useful or suited to action.
entries.definitionCN: 这一副词背后的形容词，义为实用的、适合行动的。

entries.definition: The noun for doing something repeatedly or in the usual way.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指反复做或通常的做法。

entries.definition: The quality of being useful or possible to carry out.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」。

entries.definition: Not sensible or not possible in real conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的」。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very close to a state or an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎；非常接近某种状态或数量，但还不是。

entries.definition: In effect, though not in a strict or formal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；就效果而言，而非严格或正式意义上。

entries.definition: A little less than, or a little before, something.
entries.definitionCN: 将近；比某数量略少，或比某时点略早。

entries.definition: In effect, even if not officially or literally.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；即便不是名义上或字面上如此。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adverb of practical, and its family keeps returning to action, while the sense almost grows out of in effect.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 practical 的副词，同族词反复回到行动，而「几乎」义则从「在效果上」长出。

normal.en: Practically is practical plus -ly, so its base meaning is in a practical way.
normal.cn: practically 是 practical 加 -ly，所以本义是「以实际的方式」。

normal.en: The adverb later drifted to almost: what is practically true is true for all useful purposes.
normal.cn: 这个副词后来漂到「几乎」：在实际上成立的事，对所有实际用途都成立。

normal.en: Practicality is the noun of the same family, naming the quality of being workable.
normal.cn: practicality 是同族的名词，指可行性这种性质。

normal.en: Impractical adds im- to practical and means not workable in real conditions.
normal.cn: impractical 在 practical 前加 im-，指在真实条件下行不通。

normal.en: Practically speaking is a fixed phrase that announces a judgement about real conditions.
normal.cn: practically speaking 是固定说法，用来引出对真实条件的判断。

abstract.en: Practically sits between yes and no: it says the difference is real but too small to matter.
abstract.cn: practically 站在「是」与「否」之间：它说差别确实存在，却小到无关紧要。

abstract.en: A road that is practically a river is not a river, yet no car will pass.
abstract.cn: 一条几乎成了河的路并不是河，但没有车能过去。

abstract.en: The word measures the gap between the rule and the world, then decides the gap can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量规则与世界之间的差距，然后判定这道差距可以忽略。

examples.en: By evening the road was practically a river.
examples.cn: 到了傍晚，这条路几乎成了一条河。

examples.en: It is practically impossible to finish the report tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚要写完这份报告几乎不可能。

examples.en: Practically speaking, the plan costs more than we can afford.
examples.cn: 实际上，这个计划的费用超出我们的承受能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来克提扣里」——扣得上的东西几乎都合用；practically 就是几乎、实际上。

root: 由 practical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；词干可上溯希腊语 prassein（做、行动）与 praktikos（适合行动的），经拉丁语 practicus 与古法语 pratique 传入英语。表示「几乎」的义项一般认为从「在实际效果上」的用法引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what holds in practice; the senses divide into the manner of acting, the reality of a situation, and the everyday drift to almost.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在实践中成立」；义项由此分出做事的做法、局面的实情，以及日常用法里向「几乎」的漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup standing near the edge of a table, filled to the very brim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只杯子立在桌边，水面几乎碰到杯口，只差一线就溢出。

branches.en: a cup filled to the very edge, one line short of spilling
branches.cn: 杯子几乎满到边，只差一线就溢出

branches.en: a locked drawer opened with a thin knife

branches.en: a long walk shortened to a short cut through a yard
branches.cn: 把一段远路改走穿院子的小道

intro.en: The adverb is practical plus -ly, and the whole family goes back to a Greek verb meaning to do.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 practical 加 -ly，整族词都上溯一个意为「做」的希腊动词。

latinIntro.en: Practically inherits the Latin adjective practicus and the English practical; the Latin line itself goes back to Greek praktikos, fit for action.
latinIntro.cn: practically 继承拉丁形容词 practicus 与英语 practical；这条拉丁线索本身又上溯希腊语 praktikos（适合行动的）。

definition_zh: 获得；增加；收益；（钟表）走快
definition_en: to get something useful, to increase in amount, or an increase or profit
core_image: 天平上的砝码一点点增加
scene: 她通过实习获得了宝贵的经验。 She gained valuable experience through the internship.
sceneCN: 这里 gain 是「获得」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她通过实习获得了宝贵的经验。

senses.title: Obtain something useful
senses.definition: to obtain something valuable through effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力得到有价值的东西
senses.example: She gained valuable experience through the internship.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过实习获得了宝贵的经验。
senses.why: This is the core sense of earning something.
senses.whyCN: 这是通过努力得到某物的核心义项。

senses.title: Increase in amount
senses.definition: to increase in weight, speed, or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在重量、速度或数量上增长
senses.example: He gained five kilos during the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他冬天重了五公斤。
senses.why: The word covers growth as well as earning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既涵盖获得也涵盖增长。

senses.title: Profit or increase
senses.definition: an increase in money, advantage, or value
senses.definitionCN: 金钱、优势或价值上的增长
senses.example: The company reported a small gain this year.
senses.exampleCN: 公司今年报告了小幅收益。
senses.why: As a noun it names the increase itself.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时它指增长本身。

senses.title: Run fast by a clock
senses.definition: to run ahead of the correct time, used of a clock
senses.definitionCN: 指钟表比正确时间走得快
senses.example: The old clock gains three minutes a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧钟每天快三分钟。
senses.why: A clock gains time as money gains value.
senses.whyCN: 钟表增加时间，如同金钱增加价值。

intro.en: Gain came from Old French, naming the profit of effort.
intro.cn: gain 来自古法语，指努力所得的收益。

items.en: Gaaignier meant to earn or win.
items.cn: gaaignier 意为赚取或赢得。

items.en: The word entered English as gain.
items.cn: 这个词以 gain 进入英语。

items.en: It covered both earning and growing.
items.cn: 它同时涵盖获得和增长。

items.en: Finance gave the noun a profit sense.
items.cn: 金融领域赋予名词收益义。

items.en: Clocks gain time when they run fast.
items.cn: 钟表走快时被说成 gain time。

note.en: Gain is compared with look-alike words and words for getting or profit.
note.cn: 把 gain 与形近词以及表示获得或收益的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To gain is to end up with more than you had.
normalIntro.cn: gain 就是最终比原来拥有得更多。

normal.en: She gained valuable experience through the internship.
normal.cn: 她通过实习获得了宝贵的经验。

normal.en: He gained five kilos during the winter.
normal.cn: 他冬天重了五公斤。

normal.en: The company reported a small gain this year.
normal.cn: 公司今年报告了小幅收益。

normal.en: The old clock gains three minutes a day.
normal.cn: 这座旧钟每天快三分钟。

normal.en: You gain nothing by waiting.
normal.cn: 干等不会让你得到任何东西。

abstract.en: No pain, no gain is a hard but honest rule.
abstract.cn: 不劳无获是一条严酷却诚实的规则。

abstract.en: We gain most when we give something away.
abstract.cn: 我们付出时得到的往往最多。

abstract.en: Time is the one gain no clock can hold.
abstract.cn: 时间是任何钟表都留不住的一笔所得。

examples.cn: 她通过实习获得了宝贵的经验。

examples.en: He gained five kilos during the winter.
examples.cn: 他冬天重了五公斤。

examples.en: The company reported a small gain this year.
examples.cn: 公司今年报告了小幅收益。

dict_mnemonic.text: gain 与 again、grain 形近；gain experience 是「获得经验」，no pain no gain 是「不劳无获」。

root: 经古法语 gaaignier（赚取、赢得）进入英语，核心义「通过努力使所得增加」。

sensesIntro.en: Gain means obtaining something, increasing, making a profit, or running fast of a clock.
sensesIntro.cn: gain 指获得某物、增加、取得收益，或钟表走快。

core.en: To end up with more than before.
core.cn: 最终拥有比之前更多。

branches.en: Work turns into useful experience.
branches.cn: 工作转化为有用的经验。

branches.en: Weight and speed can grow.
branches.cn: 体重和速度都能增长。

branches.en: Money shows a rise on the page.
branches.cn: 金钱在账面上显示增长。

branches.en: A clock runs ahead of true time.
branches.cn: 钟表比真实时间跑得快。

branches.en: Earning and profit share one word.
branches.cn: 获得与收益共用一个词。

intro.en: Gain builds words for earning, increase, and recovery.
intro.cn: gain 构成表示赚取、增长和重新获得的词。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Old French, not straight from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经古法语传来，并非直接来自拉丁语。

items.example: He gained the trust of the team.
The firm gains new customers daily.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司每天获得新客户。

items.example: She gained a great deal from travel.

items.exampleCN: 这个想法正在获得支持。

items.example: He found gainful work in the city.
items.exampleCN: 他在城里找到了有报酬的工作。

items.example: The biggest gainer was the small shop.
items.exampleCN: 收益最大的是那家小店。

definition_zh: 道歉；歉意；辩白；勉强的替代品
definition_en: a statement saying that one is sorry; also, in older use, a formal defense, or a very poor substitute
core_image: 一篇本为辩护的言辞，最后低头说出对不起
scene: 清晨的花店门口，送错花束的伙计把卡片翻过来看了看。 Her apology was a hand-written note tied to a bunch of white roses.
sceneCN: 这里 apology 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：表示歉意的言辞或文字）；句意为「她的道歉是一张绑在一束白玫瑰上的手写便条」。画面里有清晨的花店门口、白玫瑰和低头看卡片的伙计。

pos.zh: 名词：道歉；歉意；辩白；勉强的替代品

collocations.zh: 为……所作的道歉；勉强算作……的东西

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「道歉」
由本词加形容词后缀 -etic 构成，义为「表示歉意的」
由 apologetic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「带着歉意地」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「辩护者」，保留较古的「辩解」义

senses.title: A statement of regret
senses.definition: words or a written message saying that one is sorry for a fault or harm
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面的言辞，表示为某项过失或伤害感到抱歉
senses.example: Her apology was a hand-written note tied to a bunch of white roses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的道歉是一张绑在一束白玫瑰上的手写便条。
senses.why: The Greek word named a defense speech, but the modern noun has dropped the defense and kept only the regret, so the statement itself becomes the amends.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原本指辩护之辞，但现代名词丢掉了辩护，只留下懊悔，于是这番陈述本身就成了补偿。

senses.title: An accepted repair of a relationship
senses.definition: such a statement considered as a social act that restores good relations
senses.definitionCN: 把这类言辞视为一种恢复良好关系的社会行为
senses.example: She accepted his apology with a quiet nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点头，接受了他的道歉。
senses.why: An apology is a small ritual: since the damage cannot be undone, words are offered and then accepted in its place.
senses.whyCN: 道歉是一种小仪式：既然损害无法撤销，就用言辞顶上去，再被对方接受。

senses.title: A formal defense, old use
senses.definition: in older and formal use, a written or spoken defense of a person, belief, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 较旧与正式的用法，指为人、信念或机构所作的书面或口头辩护
senses.example: The book is an apology for the old system of guilds.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是为旧的行会制度作辩白。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense, still visible in titles and in the derived word apologist, where the speech is a shield.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义，仍见于书名与派生词 apologist 之中，那里的言辞是一面盾牌。

senses.title: A poor substitute
senses.definition: in informal and often ironic use, something that is a very inadequate example or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 非正式且常带反讽的用法，指极不像样的事物或替代品
senses.example: The so-called garden was a poor apology for a park.
senses.exampleCN: 那座所谓的花园，勉强算个公园的替代品。
senses.why: The ironic sense grows by contrast: a mere word standing in for a real thing is as weak as an apology standing in for repair.
senses.whyCN: 这个反讽义靠对比生长：仅用言辞顶替实物，就像用道歉顶替修补一样无力。

senses.title: A public or official statement
senses.definition: an official statement of regret issued by an institution or a person in public
senses.definitionCN: 由机构或个人在公众场合发布的正式致歉声明
senses.example: The airline issued a public apology for the cancelled flights.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司为取消的航班发布了公开道歉。
senses.why: When the fault is public, the repair must be public too, so the private word of regret becomes an official document.
senses.whyCN: 当过失是公开的，修补也必须公开，于是私下的懊悔之言变成一份正式文件。

intro.en: Apology comes from a Greek word for a speech of defense, and its modern sense of regret is a later turning of that word.
intro.cn: apology 来自希腊语中表示「辩护之辞」的词，它现代的「歉意」义是后来转出来的。

items.en: Apologia meant a speech in defense, built from apo- 'away from' and logos 'word, account'; Plato's defense of Socrates bore this name.
items.cn: apologia 指为辩护而作的言辞，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、论述」构成；柏拉图那篇为苏格拉底辩护的文字就叫这个名字。

items.en: Latin keeps apologia as a learned word for a formal defense or justification.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 apologia，作为表示正式辩护或申辩的学术词。

items.en: English borrows apology in the sense 'defense', and the word is at home in theology and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语借入 apology 时取「辩护」义，这个词在神学与修辞学里安家。

items.en: The sense shifts towards 'expression of regret', while the old defensive sense survives in set titles and in apologist.
items.cn: 词义转向「表达歉意」，而旧的辩护义保留在固定书名与 apologist 一词里。

items.en: The ironic sense 'poor substitute' appears in informal writing, often with the phrase an apology for.
items.cn: 反讽的「不像样的替代品」义出现在非正式文字里，常与短语 an apology for 连用。

items.en: The everyday meaning is simply 'a statement of regret'; the other senses are marked as formal, historical, or ironic.
items.cn: 日常含义就是「致歉的言辞」；其余义项则被标为正式、历史或反讽用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family; the near-meaning group gathers words for regret, defense and substitute.
note.cn: 形近组收由它派生的一族词；近义组收表示懊悔、辩护与替代品的词。

entries.definition: A reason offered to justify a fault, often weaker than an apology.

entries.definitionCN: 对过失或罪行的公开承认，比 apology 更重，强调「说出事实」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek 'defense speech' history and the frames the noun actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的希腊语「辩护之辞」历史，以及这个名词实际使用的句式。

normal.en: The skeleton is apo plus logos: a speech that turns the charge away.
normal.cn: 骨架是 apo 加 logos：一番把指控转开的言辞。

normal.en: The old title still means defense: Plato's Apology defends Socrates.
normal.cn: 旧时的书名仍是辩护义：柏拉图的《申辩》为苏格拉底辩护。

normal.en: The common frame is make an apology or accept an apology.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 make an apology 或 accept an apology。

normal.en: The ironic frame is an apology for: a poor apology for a meal is barely a meal.
normal.cn: 反讽搭配是 an apology for：说一顿饭只是勉强的替代品，就是说它几乎不算饭。

normal.en: The family keeps both faces: an apologist defends, an apologize confesses.
normal.cn: 这一族保留两副面孔：apologist 在辩护，apologize 在认错。

abstract.en: Picture a note tied to flowers: the smallest object can carry the whole repair.
abstract.cn: 想象一张绑在花上的便条：最小的物件也能承载整场修补。

abstract.en: The word is a hand extended after a break, waiting to be taken.
abstract.cn: 这个词是断裂之后伸出的一只手，等着被握住。

abstract.en: In its ironic use the hand is empty: a word pretending to be a thing.
abstract.cn: 在反讽用法里这只手是空的：一个词假装成一件实物。

examples.en: She accepted his apology with a quiet nod.
examples.cn: 她轻轻点头，接受了他的道歉。

examples.en: The manager offered a sincere apology to every guest.
examples.cn: 经理向每位客人真诚地道了歉。

examples.en: His apology for the mistake arrived a week too late.
examples.cn: 他为那次错误所作的道歉晚了一周才到。

root: apology 来自希腊语 apologia「辩护之辞」，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、论述」构成，经拉丁语 apologia 进入英语。十六世纪英语仍取「辩护」义，用于神学与修辞；十八世纪转向「表达歉意」，旧义退守固定书名与 apologist；十九世纪出现反讽义「不像样的替代品」，常作 an apology for；现代日常义就是「致歉的言辞」。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from a defense speech that became a confession: the spoken regret, the social repair, the old defense, the ironic substitute, and the official public statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从一篇转为认错的辩护之辞展开：口头的懊悔、社会性的修补、旧的辩护义、反讽的替代品，以及正式的公开声明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a defense speech lowered into a confession, then handed over like a note.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篇辩护之辞被放低成认错，再像便条一样递出去。

branches.en: THE REGRET LINE: the defense is gone and only sorrow remains.
branches.cn: 懊悔线：辩护没有了，只剩歉意。

branches.en: THE REPAIR LINE: words are offered and accepted in place of damage.
branches.cn: 修补线：用言辞顶替损害，并被对方接受。

branches.en: THE OLD SHIELD LINE: the Greek defense survives in titles and in apologist.
branches.cn: 旧盾牌线：希腊语的辩护义活在书名与 apologist 里。

branches.en: THE IRONY LINE: a word pretending to be a thing is a poor apology for it.
branches.cn: 反讽线：一个假装成实物的词，就是它勉强的替代品。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC LINE: private regret becomes an official document.
branches.cn: 公开线：私下的懊悔变成一份正式文件。

intro.en: Apology is a classical borrowing, so its parts are Greek and Latin rather than native English.
intro.cn: apology 是古典借词，因此它的构件来自希腊语与拉丁语，而非本族英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin link is direct: apologia carried the Greek word into English, and the derived family keeps the same skeleton.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一环是直接的：apologia 把这个希腊词带进英语，派生的一族保留着同样的骨架。

intro.en: Worth turned into an adjective with -able, with a negative and a privative partner close by.
intro.cn: 把「值得」用 -able 变成形容词，旁边还有否定与「无」两个伙伴。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, to be worth, gives value; adding -able gives the adjective, adding in- gives invaluable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere（值得）给出 value；加 -able 成形容词，加 in- 成 invaluable。

items.example: Value is what the adjective measures.
items.exampleCN: value 是这个形容词衡量的东西。

items.example: The root val- sits behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 val- 支撑整个词族。

items.example: Worth is the plain English twin.
items.exampleCN: worth 是朴素的英语孪生词。

definition_zh: 挣得；赚得；赢得；博得；生（利息）
definition_en: to get money or something else of value in return for work or effort, or to gain a quality such as respect because one deserves it
core_image: 汗湿的手把一天的工钱攥紧，钱是自己挣来的
scene: 砖窑的日头落下去，工人领到当天的工钱。 Two weeks of night shifts earned him enough for the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 earn 是「挣得（钱）」（第 1 个义项：靠劳动换取报酬）；句意为两周夜班让他挣够了房租。图中可辨识物件：砖窑、工钱、落日。

pos.zh: 动词：挣得；赚得；赢得；博得；生（利息）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「收入；收益」
由本词加施事后缀构成，义为「挣钱者；收入来源」
由否定前缀与本词加后缀构成，义为「非劳动所得的」

senses.title: To get money by working
senses.definition: to receive money in return for work or services
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或服务而获得钱财
senses.example: She earns more in a week than her father did in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她一周挣得比她父亲当年一个月挣得还多。
senses.why: Old English earnian already meant to earn wages; money is what the work is exchanged for.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 earnian 已经表示「挣得工钱」；钱就是劳动所换来的东西。

senses.title: To gain something by merit
senses.definition: to gain a quality such as respect, trust or a place because one deserves it
senses.definitionCN: 因自己配得上而获得尊重、信任或某个位置等
senses.example: He earned the trust of every farmer in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢得了山谷里每一位农夫的信任。
senses.why: The same verb moves from wages to worth: effort and character are the labour that earns trust or respect.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从工钱移到价值：努力与品格就是挣得信任或尊重的劳动。

senses.title: To yield as interest or profit
senses.definition: to produce interest or profit, said of money that is saved or invested
senses.definitionCN: 指被存下或投入的钱产生利息或利润
senses.example: The account earns four percent interest each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个账户每年生百分之四的利息。
senses.why: Money set aside is imagined as working on your behalf, so it too earns something for you.
senses.whyCN: 存起来的钱被想象成替你干活，于是它也能为你挣得些什么。

intro.en: Earn is native Old English, and its earliest sense was closer to 'deserve' than to 'take home a wage'.
intro.cn: earn 是古英语本族词，最早的含义更接近「应得」，而不是「领回工资」。

items.en: A wider origin beyond Germanic is often proposed but not settled, so it is best treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之外的更早来源常有推测，但尚无定论，宜视为不确定。

items.en: A Germanic verb with the sense of earning or deserving is reconstructed from the related forms.
items.cn: 根据相关形式可重构出一个表示「挣得、应得」的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: Earnian meant to earn, deserve or merit something through effort.
items.cn: earnian 意为靠努力挣得、应得或配得上某物。

items.en: The verb narrowed toward wages and money while the merit sense survived in phrases.
items.cn: 这个动词向「工钱、钱财」收窄，而「应得」的意思在短语里留存下来。

items.en: Earn respect and earn interest show the old merit sense and the newer financial sense side by side.
items.cn: earn respect 与 earn interest 并列展示出较旧的「应得」义与较新的财务义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that sound or look close but mean something else; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for getting value.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写接近但意思不同的词；近义组收表示「取得价值」的动词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to long for something strongly.
The organ of hearing, or the head of a grain plant.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官，或谷物的穗头。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: To obtain something, often through effort or over time.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物，常指经努力或随时间而来。

entries.definition: To be worthy of something because of one's actions or qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 因行为或品质而配得上某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the word from wages to trust, then to money that works on its own.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着这个词从工钱走到信任，再走到自己会干活的钱。

normal.en: Earn begins as 'deserve', then settles on 'take home pay'.
normal.cn: earn 起初是「应得」，后来落在「领回家的钱」上。

normal.en: Work is exchanged for money, which is the plainest kind of earning.
normal.cn: 劳动换来钱财，这是最直白的一种挣得。

normal.en: Trust and respect are wages paid in another currency.
normal.cn: 信任与尊重是用另一种货币支付的工钱。

normal.en: Money in a savings account is said to earn because it is imagined as working.
normal.cn: 储蓄账户里的钱被说成 earn，因为它被想象成在干活。

normal.en: Keep yearn apart: one word stretches toward what is absent, the other collects what is due.
normal.cn: 把 yearn 分清楚：一个词伸向缺席之物，另一个词收下应得之物。

abstract.en: Picture a coin weighed on one side by hours of work and on the other by a printed wage.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，一边压着数小时劳动，一边压着印好的工资数。

abstract.en: The same scales can weigh trust, a place at a table, or interest on a deposit.
abstract.cn: 同一架天平也能称信任、桌上的一席之位，或存款的利息。

abstract.en: Earn means the balance was paid for, not simply received.
abstract.cn: earn 意味着这份平衡是付过代价换来的，而不是白得的。

examples.en: She earns more in a week than her father did in a month.
examples.cn: 她一周挣得比她父亲当年一个月挣得还多。

examples.en: He earned the trust of every farmer in the valley.
examples.cn: 他赢得了山谷里每一位农夫的信任。

examples.en: The account earns four percent interest each year.
examples.cn: 这个账户每年生百分之四的利息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄恩」——夜里搬砖，天亮攥住自己换来的钱

root: 古英语 earnian「应得、挣得」来自日耳曼语层，同族形式在德语与荷兰语中表示收获或劳作报酬；日耳曼语之外的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of earn all describe value obtained because something was given first: labour for money, effort for trust, and savings for interest.
sensesIntro.cn: earn 的三个义项都在描述「先付出、后取得」的价值：劳动换钱、努力换信任、存款换利息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin is weighed against hours of work, and the two sides come level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币与数小时劳动放在天平两端，最后持平。

branches.en: THE WAGE: hours of work are exchanged for money.
branches.cn: 工钱线：数小时劳动被换成钱财。

branches.en: THE MERIT: effort and character are exchanged for trust or respect.
branches.cn: 功绩线：努力与品格被换成信任或尊重。

branches.en: THE YIELD: saved money is imagined as working and returning interest.
branches.cn: 收益线：存下的钱被想象成在干活，并带回利息。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: in both cases something must be given before the gain is paid out.
branches.cn: 条件线：两种情况下都得先付出，收获才会被支付。

branches.en: THE RETURN: what comes back is proportional to what was put in, whether labour or capital.
branches.cn: 回报线：回来的东西与投入的东西相称，无论投入的是劳动还是资本。

intro.en: Earn is a native Germanic verb; English adds ordinary suffixes and one negative prefix, plus a few fixed phrases.
intro.cn: earn 是日耳曼语本族动词，英语加上普通后缀、一个否定前缀，以及若干固定短语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is involved; the related forms belong to the Germanic languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁语来源，相关形式属于日耳曼语族。

items.example: The Old English verb already joined pay and merit.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词已经把「报酬」与「应得」合在一起。

items.example: The form is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式是重构的，并非有记录的原词。

definition_zh: 地狱；见鬼；到底
definition_en: a place of punishment after death, or a word used for swearing and emphasis
core_image: 地下燃着火焰、罪人受罚的地方
scene: 他相信坏人死后会下地狱。 He believed that bad people go to hell after death.
sceneCN: 这里 hell 是「地狱」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他相信坏人死后会下地狱。

senses.title: Place of punishment
senses.definition: a place where bad people are said to be punished after death
senses.definitionCN: 传说中坏人死后受罚的地方
senses.example: He believed that bad people go to hell after death.
senses.exampleCN: 他相信坏人死后会下地狱。
senses.why: This is the old religious sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词古老的宗教义项。

senses.title: Swear word
senses.definition: used in angry speech as a swear word
senses.definitionCN: 在恼怒时用作咒骂语
senses.example: Oh hell, I forgot my keys.
senses.exampleCN: 见鬼，我忘带钥匙了。
senses.why: Anger borrows the worst place people can name.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒时会借用人们能想到的最糟的地方。

senses.title: For emphasis
senses.definition: used after question words to add force
senses.definitionCN: 用在疑问词后加强语气
senses.example: What the hell are you doing?
senses.exampleCN: 你到底在干什么？
senses.why: The swear word becomes a way to push a question.
senses.whyCN: 咒骂词变成了加重疑问的说法。

intro.en: Hell is a Germanic word for a hidden world under the earth.
intro.cn: hell 是日耳曼语词，指地下隐蔽的世界。

items.en: The root meant a hidden or covered place.
items.cn: 该词根意为被遮盖的地方。

items.en: Hell named the underworld of the dead.
items.cn: hell 指死者的地下世界。

items.en: The Norse Hel named a goddess and her realm.
items.cn: 古北欧语 Hel 既是女神也是她的国度。

items.en: Hell became the general word for a place of punishment.
items.cn: hell 成为惩罚之地的通称。

items.en: Hell turned into a swear word and an intensifier.
items.cn: hell 发展为咒骂词和加强语气的词。

note.en: Hell is compared with look-alike words and with words for terrible places.
note.cn: 把 hell 与形近词以及表示可怕之地的词作比较。

entries.definition: to make healthy again
the past form of hold
the wheel or handle of a ship
the world of the dead
a large fierce fire
a very deep hole

normalIntro.en: Hell is the dark place below, and also a word for anger and emphasis.
normalIntro.cn: hell 是地下的黑暗之地，也是表达恼怒和加强语气的词。

normal.en: He believed that bad people go to hell.
normal.cn: 他相信坏人会下地狱。

normal.en: Oh hell, I forgot my keys.
normal.cn: 见鬼，我忘带钥匙了。

normal.en: The kitchen was hot as hell.
normal.cn: 厨房里热得要命。

normal.en: War can turn a city into hell.
normal.cn: 战争能把城市变成地狱。

abstract.en: Hell is often a place people build for each other.
abstract.cn: 地狱常常是人给人造出来的地方。

abstract.en: The road to hell is wide and easy to walk.
abstract.cn: 通往地狱的路又宽又好走。

abstract.en: Even hell is said to have its own weather.
abstract.cn: 据说连地狱也有自己的天气。

examples.en: He believed that bad people go to hell after death.
examples.cn: 他相信坏人死后会下地狱。

examples.en: Oh hell, I forgot my keys.
examples.cn: 见鬼，我忘带钥匙了。

examples.en: What the hell are you doing?
examples.cn: 你到底在干什么？

dict_mnemonic.text: hell 是「地狱」，也可作咒骂的「见鬼」，还可用在疑问词后加强语气，如 what the hell（到底）；go to hell 是下地狱，raise hell 是大吵大闹。

root: 来自古英语 hell，与古北欧语 Hel 同源，本义指被遮盖的地下世界；由死者的居所引申为惩罚之地，再发展出咒骂与加强语气的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Hell is a place of punishment, a swear word, or a way to add force to a question.
sensesIntro.cn: hell 是地狱、咒骂语，或加强疑问语气的词。

core.en: A hidden world below, which became a place of punishment.
core.cn: 地下的隐蔽世界，后来成为惩罚之地。

branches.en: He believed that bad people go to hell.
branches.cn: 他相信坏人会下地狱。

branches.en: The worst place becomes the strongest word.

intro.en: Hell forms a small family of words for terrible places and fierce people.
intro.cn: hell 构成一小族词，表示可怕的地方和凶悍的人。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: He talked about hell in his sermon.

items.exampleCN: 他们宣讲地狱之火与末日。

items.example: The boy was a famous hellraiser.
items.exampleCN: 那男孩是出了名的捣蛋鬼。

items.example: The flood made a hell on earth.
items.exampleCN: 洪水把那里变成了人间地狱。

definition_zh: 最精彩的部分；高亮；强调
definition_en: the best or most important part of something, or a bright area in a picture
core_image: 舞台灯光落在全场最亮的那一小块
scene: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。 The highlight of the show was a duet.
sceneCN: 这里 highlight 是「最精彩的部分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。

senses.title: Best part
senses.definition: the best or most exciting part of an event
senses.definitionCN: 事件中最精彩或最激动人心的部分
senses.example: The highlight of the show was a duet.
senses.exampleCN: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常用的日常义项。

senses.title: Bright area
senses.definition: the brightest part of a picture or scene
senses.definitionCN: 画面或场景中最亮的部分
senses.example: Keep the highlights in the photo soft.
senses.exampleCN: 让照片中的高光部分保持柔和。
senses.why: The word keeps its literal sense of bright light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「明亮的光」这一本义。

senses.title: Emphasize
senses.definition: to draw attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 引起人们对某事物的注意
senses.example: The report highlights the need for change.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调了变革的必要性。
senses.why: As a verb it means to make something stand out.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时表示让某事物突显出来。

intro.cn: highlight 由 high 和 light 两个词组合而成。

items.en: Heah meant high or tall.
items.cn: heah 意为高的或高大的。

items.en: Leoht meant light.
items.cn: leoht 意为光。

items.en: High and light often appeared together.
items.cn: high 和 light 经常一起出现。

items.en: Highlight first named the brightest part of a painting.
items.cn: highlight 最初指画中最亮的部分。

items.cn: 后来 highlight 指最精彩的部分。

items.en: As a verb it now means to emphasize.
items.cn: 作动词时，它现在表示强调。

note.en: Highlight is compared with look-alike compounds and with words for the best moment.
