definition_zh: 迹象；表明；指示；（医学）体征、适应证；读数
definition_en: a sign that shows something is true or likely, or the act of pointing something out
core_image: 一根手指指向远处，所有人顺着它看过去
scene: 客厅窗前，全家人盯着电视里的台风路径图，画面一帧帧更新。 There was no indication that the storm would turn inland until the barometer fell.
sceneCN: 这里 indication 是「迹象」（第 1 个义项：显示某事可能属实的信号）；句意：在气压计下降之前，没有任何迹象表明风暴会转向内陆。图中可辨识物件：气压计指针、窗外压低的云层、指向地图的手指。

pos.zh: 迹象；表明；指示；体征；适应证

senses.title: A sign that something is so
senses.definition: a piece of evidence that suggests a fact or a likely development
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某事实或可能发展的证据
senses.example: There is no indication that the trend will reverse.
senses.exampleCN: 没有迹象表明这一趋势会逆转。
senses.why: Indicare means 'to point out'. An indication is a finger pointed at a fact, and the viewer must still read what it points to.
senses.whyCN: indicare 意为“指出”。indication 就是指向事实的一根手指，而观看者仍须读懂它指向什么。

senses.title: The act of pointing something out
senses.definition: the act of stating or showing that something is the case
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或显示某事如此的行为
senses.example: His indication of the exit saved us time.
senses.exampleCN: 他指出出口，替我们省了时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation makes this the act itself, not the sign. Someone performs the pointing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 使这个词指行为本身，而非标志。是某人在做指向动作。

senses.title: A medical sign
senses.definition: in medicine, an observable sign that points to a condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指向某种病情的可观察体征
senses.example: Fever is one indication of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发热是感染的一种体征。
senses.why: A clinical sign is a finger aimed at a hidden cause. The cause remains invisible; only the pointing is visible.
senses.whyCN: 临床体征是一根指向隐藏病因的手指。病因仍然不可见，可见的只有这次指向。

senses.title: A reading on an instrument
senses.definition: a value shown by a gauge or meter
senses.definitionCN: 计量仪表显示的数值
senses.example: The dial gave no indication of pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 表盘没有显示压力读数。
senses.why: The needle is a literal finger on a scale. The instrument indicates, and the reading is the indication.
senses.whyCN: 指针就是落在刻度上的一根真实手指。仪表在指示，读数就是这次指示。

senses.title: A signal or gesture
senses.definition: a gesture or signal intended to convey a message
senses.definitionCN: 意在传达讯息的手势或信号
senses.example: A nod was his indication that we should begin.
senses.exampleCN: 一个点头就是他示意我们开始的信号。
senses.why: Here the pointing is bodily and immediate. Nothing is written; the message is delivered by a movement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向是身体性的、即时的。没有文字，讯息由一个动作递出。

senses.title: A hint in speech or manner
senses.definition: a subtle hint given in conversation rather than a direct statement
senses.definitionCN: 交谈中给出的细微暗示，而非直接陈述
senses.example: He gave a slight indication that he was unhappy.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了个细微暗示，表示自己不高兴。
senses.why: The finger is only half raised. The word marks a signal deliberately kept below the level of a statement.
senses.whyCN: 手指只抬起一半。这个词标记的是一个被刻意压在陈述线以下的信号。

senses.title: Evidence pointing to a conclusion
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is every indication', evidence strong enough to support an expectation
senses.definitionCN: 在“种种迹象表明”这一说法中，强到足以支持某种预期的证据
senses.example: There is every indication that the talks will succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 种种迹象表明会谈将会成功。
senses.why: The phrase weighs a set of fingers all pointing the same way. Indication becomes the collective direction of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法称量一组都指向同一方向的手指。indication 成了证据的集体方向。

senses.title: A reason to use a treatment
senses.definition: in medicine, a condition that makes a particular treatment appropriate
senses.definitionCN: 医学中使某种治疗变得合适的病情
senses.example: The scan gave a clear indication for surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描结果给出了明确的手术适应证。
senses.why: Here the pointing goes the other way: the condition points at the treatment, licensing the doctor to act.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向反了过来：病情指向治疗，从而授权医生行动。

intro.en: Indication comes from Latin indicare, 'to point out'. It is built from in- plus dicare, 'to proclaim', and is related to index, the pointing finger. Every sense keeps that gesture: something is aimed at, and the viewer must read the aim.
intro.cn: indication 来自拉丁语 indicare“指出”。它由 in- 加 dicare“宣告”构成，与 index（食指、索引）同族。每个义项都保留那个手势：某物被指向，而观看者必须读懂指向。

items.en: Dicare meant 'to proclaim, to dedicate'. Its relation to dicere 'to say' is generally accepted, but the exact prehistoric division between the two verbs is uncertain.
items.cn: dicare 意为“宣告、奉献”。它与 dicere“说”的关系一般被接受，但两个动词在史前期的具体分化来源不确定。

items.en: Index meant 'a pointer, a sign, the forefinger'. The plural indices kept the same stem that produced indicate. This is why an index and an indication both point.
items.cn: index 意为“指示者、标志、食指”。复数 indices 保留的词干正产生了 indicate。索引与迹象都指方向，原因就在这里。

items.en: In- plus dicare gave indicare, 'to point out, to show, to give a sign'. The verb was used of fingers, of evidence and of prices.
items.cn: in- 加 dicare 构成 indicare“指出、显示、给出信号”。这个动词既用于手指，也用于证据与价格。

items.en: The noun indicatio named the act of pointing out. Latin medical writers already used it for symptoms that point to a disease.
items.cn: 名词 indicatio 指指出某物的行为。拉丁医学作者已用它指指向疾病的症状。

items.en: English borrowed indication through French. Early uses concerned both 'a hint' and 'a symptom', and the medical sense has never left.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 indication。早期用法兼指“暗示”与“症状”，医学义从未离开这个单词。

items.en: Clinical indication, indication for surgery and instrument indications fixed the word in medicine and engineering, where a sign licenses an action.
items.cn: 临床指征、手术适应证与仪表读数使这个词固定于医学与工程，在这些领域里，一个信号就是行动的依据。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, this noun and the instrument noun. The meaning group compares words for signs and evidence.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、本名词与仪器名词；词义组比较表示迹象与证据的词。

entries.definition: to point out or show. It is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指出或显示。它是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: a gauge or a measurable sign. It is the thing that points, while indication is the pointing or the pointed-at fact.
entries.definitionCN: 仪表或可测量的标志。它是做指向的东西，而 indication 是指向动作或被指的事实。

entries.definition: an alphabetical list, a number expressing change, or the forefinger. It shares the pointing stem.
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排列的清单、表示变化的数字，或食指。它共享“指向”的词干。

entries.definition: anything that suggests the presence of something. It is the broad everyday word; indication is more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示某物存在的任何东西。它是宽泛的日常词，indication 更正式。

entries.definition: a change in the body that points to a disease. It matches sense 03 specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 身体上指向疾病的变化。它专门对应第 3 义项。

entries.definition: facts offered to support a claim. It is stronger than indication and carries the weight of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 为支持某主张而提供的事实。它比 indication 更强，带有证明的分量。

entries.definition: an indirect suggestion. It is close to sense 06 and is always deliberately understated.
entries.definitionCN: 间接的提示。它接近第 6 义项，且总是刻意压低力度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build indication from in- plus dicare, 'to proclaim', and keep the pointing finger and the index card in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 in- 加 dicare“宣告”搭起 indication，并让指向的手指与索引卡始终在眼前。

normal.en: See in- + dicare: to proclaim towards something. An indication is a proclamation aimed at a fact.
normal.cn: 看成 in- 加 dicare：朝某物宣告。indication 就是指向某个事实的宣告。

normal.en: Picture a finger pointing at a distant hill: the hill is the fact, the finger is the indication.
normal.cn: 想象一根手指指向远处的山：山是事实，手指是迹象。

normal.en: An index is a book's pointing finger; an indication is evidence's pointing finger.
normal.cn: 索引是书的指向手指；迹象是证据的指向手指。

normal.en: In medicine, a symptom points at a cause the doctor cannot yet see.
normal.cn: 在医学里，症状指向医生尚看不见的病因。

normal.en: When there is every indication, many fingers point the same way.
normal.cn: 当“种种迹象表明”时，是许多手指都指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Keep one gesture: aim, and let another read the aim.
abstract.cn: 只记一个手势：指过去，让别人读懂所指。

abstract.en: Treat the word as weaker than proof and stronger than a guess.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作比证据弱、比猜测强的东西。

abstract.en: Notice that the same word covers a raised finger and a falling barometer: both are pointers.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个词既覆盖抬起的手指，也覆盖下降的气压计：两者都是指向器。

examples.en: The survey gives a useful indication of public mood.
examples.cn: 这项调查为了解公众情绪提供了有用的迹象。

examples.en: There is every indication that the policy is working.
examples.cn: 种种迹象表明这项政策正在奏效。

examples.en: The doctor found no indication for further surgery.
examples.cn: 医生认为没有进一步手术的适应证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“印地开神”：印度街头的开示神像用手一指，众人顺着看过去——这就是指示、迹象。

root: 拉丁语 indicare“指出、显示”（in- 朝向 + dicare 宣告），名词 indicatio；与 index“食指、索引”同出“指向”词干。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of indication is a pointing. Sometimes the finger is a symptom, sometimes a needle, sometimes a nod, sometimes a half-raised hint, sometimes a whole body of evidence, and sometimes a condition that points at a treatment. The word never contains the conclusion; it contains the direction in which to look.
sensesIntro.cn: indication 的每个义项都是一次指向。有时手指是症状，有时是仪表指针，有时是一个点头，有时是抬到一半的暗示，有时是整组证据，有时是病情指向某种治疗。这个词从不包含结论，它包含的是该往哪里看。

core.en: A pointing that tells another where to look.
core.cn: 一次指向，告诉别人该往哪里看。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: signs and the collective weight of signs.
branches.cn: 证据：迹象与迹象的集体分量。

branches.en: GESTURE: the act of pointing and a signal given by hand.
branches.cn: 手势：指向动作与用手给出的信号。

branches.en: HINT: a sign deliberately kept below the level of a statement.
branches.cn: 暗示：被刻意压在陈述线以下的信号。

branches.en: MEDICINE: a symptom pointing to a cause, a condition licensing treatment.
branches.cn: 医学：指向病因的症状，以及授权治疗的病情。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a needle's reading.
branches.cn: 仪表：指针的读数。

intro.en: Indication is indicare plus -atio. The items below gather the pointing family, including index, which looks different but shares the same stem.
intro.cn: indication 是 indicare 加 -atio。下列条目汇总“指向”词族，包括形似不同却共享同一词干的 index。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the pointing verb and the pointer noun. They explain why an index and an indication belong to one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出指向动词与指示者名词。它们解释了为什么索引与迹象属于同一家族。

items.meaning: a sign; the act of pointing out
items.example: The indication was easy to miss.
items.exampleCN: 这个迹象很容易被忽略。

items.example: The figures indicate a slow recovery.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字表明复苏缓慢。

items.example: The indicator moved into the red zone.
items.exampleCN: 指示器进入了红色区域。

items.example: The tone is indicative of trouble.

items.meaning: a list or a number that points to change
items.meaningCN: 指向变化的清单或数字

items.structure: plural of index, from Latin indices
items.example: Both indices point to slower growth.
items.exampleCN: 两个指数都指向增长放缓。

items.meaning: pointing to context, as a word like 'here'
items.meaningCN: 指向语境的，如“这里”这类词

items.meaning: in a way that serves as a sign
items.exampleCN: 这个样本小得只能算个示意。

definition_zh: 退休；退役；退下
definition_en: to stop working because of age, or to move away to a quiet place
core_image: 一位老人合上办公室的门，慢慢走向安静的院子
scene: 在这所学校教了三十年书后，她今年夏天退休了。 After teaching at this school for thirty years, she retired this summer.
sceneCN: 这里 retire 是「退休」（第 1 个义项：因年龄原因停止工作）；句意：在这所学校教了三十年书后，她今年夏天退休了。

senses.title: Stop working
senses.definition: to leave your job because you have reached a certain age
senses.definitionCN: 因达到一定年龄而离开工作岗位
senses.example: My father retired at sixty.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲六十岁退休。
senses.why: The French source means to withdraw, so retiring is stepping back from work.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为撤退，因此退休就是从工作中退下来。

senses.title: Leave a sport or service
senses.definition: to stop taking part in a sport or leave military service
senses.definitionCN: 停止参加体育运动或离开军队服役
senses.example: The champion retired from tennis last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冠军去年从网坛退役。
senses.why: Leaving a public career is another form of withdrawing.
senses.whyCN: 离开公开的职业生涯，是另一种撤退。

senses.title: Withdraw to rest
senses.definition: to go away to a quiet place, especially to rest or sleep
senses.definitionCN: 到一个安静的地方去，尤其是休息或睡觉
senses.example: The guests retired to their rooms after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后客人们各自回房休息。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to draw back, which survives in formal use.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是「退回」，这一用法在正式语境中保留下来。

intro.en: Retire comes from French retirer, to draw back, from tirer, to pull.
intro.cn: retire 源自法语 retirer（退回），由 tirer（拉）构成。

items.en: Tirer means to pull or draw.
items.cn: tirer 意为拉或拖。

items.en: Retirer means to draw back.
items.cn: retirer 意向往后撤。

items.en: Retire first means withdraw to a private place.
items.cn: retire 最初指退到私密之处。

items.en: The word comes to mean leaving work at a certain age.
items.cn: 这个词后来指到一定年龄离开工作。

items.en: Athletes also retire from competition.
items.cn: 运动员也会从比赛中退役。

note.en: Retire is close to withdraw and resign, but implies age or long service.
note.cn: retire 与撤退、辞职相近，但强调年龄或长期服务。

entries.definition: the state of having retired
no longer working
someone who has retired
to officially leave a job
to move away from a place or activity
to leave an important position

normalIntro.en: Retire is re- plus tire, pull: pull yourself back from work.
normalIntro.cn: retire 是 re- 加 tire（拉）：把自己从工作中拉回来。

normal.en: Retire from work means leave your job for good.
normal.cn: retire from work 意为永久离开工作。

normal.en: Retire early means stop working sooner than usual.
normal.cn: retire early 意为比通常更早停止工作。

normal.en: Soldiers retire from the army.
normal.cn: 军人从军队退役。

normal.en: Retire to bed is a formal way to say go to sleep.
normal.cn: retire to bed 是「就寝」的正式说法。

normal.en: Compare resign: resign is a choice at any age, retire usually follows long service.
normal.cn: 对比 resign：resign 任何年龄都可主动辞职，retire 通常指长期服务后退休。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing softly on a long career.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在漫长职业生涯后轻轻合上。

abstract.en: Imagine an armchair waiting by a quiet window.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子在安静的窗边等候。

abstract.en: Think of an athlete laying down a racket for the last time.
abstract.cn: 想象运动员最后一次放下球拍。

examples.en: She plans to retire next spring.
examples.cn: 她计划明年春天退休。

examples.en: The general retired after forty years of service.
examples.cn: 这位将军服役四十年后退役。

examples.en: We retired to the garden when the sun went down.
examples.cn: 太阳落山后，我们退到花园里休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ tire（拉）」——把一直往前奔的自己往回拉，就是退下来、退休；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 re-（回）＋ tirer（拉）→ retirer（退回）→ retire，核心义「从工作或人群中退回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Retire first means leave work at a certain age, then leave a sport or service, and finally withdraw to rest.
sensesIntro.cn: retire 先指到龄离开工作，再指从运动或军旅中退出，最后指退下休息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: closing an office door and walking toward a quiet yard.
core.cn: 核心意象：合上办公室的门，走向安静的院子。

branches.en: Leaving a job at a certain age is the main sense.
branches.cn: 到龄离开工作是主要义项。

branches.en: Athletes and soldiers also retire.
branches.cn: 运动员和军人也会退役。

branches.en: The old sense of withdrawing survives in formal speech.
branches.cn: 「退回」的古老含义在正式语言中保留。

branches.en: Retiring from work is a withdrawal into private life.
branches.cn: 从工作退休就是退回私人生活。

branches.en: A retired athlete steps back from public competition.
branches.cn: 退役运动员从公开赛事中退下。

intro.en: Retire has a French shape: re- plus tirer, to pull.
intro.cn: retire 带着法语形态：re- 加 tirer（拉）。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word comes through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词根，是经法语传入的。

items.example: Retired describes a person who has left work.
items.exampleCN: retired 描述已经离开工作的人。

items.example: A retiree has left work for good.
items.exampleCN: retiree 指永久离开工作的人。

definition_zh: 贡献；捐助；促成；投稿
definition_en: to give money, ideas or effort to help a group or a result, or to write for a publication
core_image: 几只手把各自的硬币放进同一只罐子
scene: 募捐箱摆在门口，路过的人陆续往里放钱。 Everyone contributed something to the fund.
sceneCN: 这里 contribute 指「捐助」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的拿出钱物或力气）；句意是每个人都为这笔基金捐了一些。

senses.title: To give a share
senses.definition: to give money, goods or effort to a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同的目的拿出钱物或力气
senses.example: Each family contributed food for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 每户人家都为宴席出了食物。
senses.why: A shared table is filled one dish at a time.
senses.whyCN: 共同的餐桌，是一道菜一道菜填满的。

senses.title: To help cause
senses.definition: to be one of the causes of a result
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个结果的原因之一
senses.example: Poor sleep contributes to low grades.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足会拉低成绩。
senses.why: Big outcomes are rarely made by one hand alone.
senses.whyCN: 大的结果很少只由一只手造成。

senses.title: To write for a publication
senses.definition: to send writing to a paper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 把文字作品寄给报刊
senses.example: She contributes a column every month.
senses.exampleCN: 她每月写一篇专栏。
senses.why: A page also has a table that others fill.
senses.whyCN: 一个版面也有别人来填的餐桌。

intro.en: Contribute comes from Latin contribuere, to bring together as a share, built from com-, together, and tribuere, to allot.
intro.cn: contribute 来自拉丁语 contribuere（把份额凑到一起），由 com-（一起）与 tribuere（分配）构成。

items.en: Tribuere meant to divide out or assign to each.
items.cn: tribuere 意为分发或分给各人。

items.en: Contribuere meant to bring shares into one common fund.
items.cn: contribuere 意为把各份凑进同一个公库。

items.en: The noun contributio named the pooling of shares.
items.cn: 名词 contributio 指各份的汇集。

items.en: French contribuer kept the sense of giving a part.
items.cn: 法语 contribuer 保留了拿出一份的意思。

items.en: English contribute widened to effort and ideas.
items.cn: 英语 contribute 扩大到力气与主意。

items.en: It also means writing for a shared page.
items.cn: 它也指为共同的版面写稿。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin allotting base tribut-, and the meaning group names other words for giving to a shared end.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的分配词基 tribut-，近义组列出其他表示为共同目标出力的词。

entries.definition: something given to a shared effort
a person who gives or writes for others
to hand something out to many people
to give money or goods to a cause
to put something in with the rest
to provide what is needed

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with coins dropped into one jar, then move to a small cause of a big result and a column sent to a paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从投进同一只罐子的硬币开始，再到大结果的小成因，最后到寄给报刊的专栏。

normal.en: Con- is together and tribute is a share, so contribute is putting your share in.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tribute 是一份，contribute 就是把你那一份放进去。

normal.en: Many small coins make one full jar.
normal.cn: 许多小硬币装满一只罐子。

normal.en: Sleep can contribute to a grade without ever writing an exam.
normal.cn: 睡眠从没参加过考试，却能影响成绩。

normal.en: A column is also a dish brought to a shared table.
normal.cn: 一篇专栏也是端到公共餐桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Give a part, and the whole grows.
normal.cn: 给出一份，整体就长了一点。

abstract.en: Picture five hands opening over one jar.
abstract.cn: 想象五只手在同一只罐子上方张开。

abstract.en: Picture one drip feeding a whole bucket.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水喂满一整只桶。

abstract.en: Picture a page filled by many different pens.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸由许多不同的笔写满。

examples.en: Everyone contributed a little money.
examples.cn: 每个人都捐了一点钱。

examples.en: Wind contributed to the spread of the fire.
examples.cn: 风助长了火势的蔓延。

examples.en: He contributes to a science magazine.
examples.cn: 他为一家科学杂志撰稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contribute 记成 con（一起）加 tribute（给出的一份）：大家各出一份凑到一起，就是贡献。

root: 源自拉丁语 contribuere（把份额凑到一起），由 con-（一起）与 tribuere（分配）构成，后指贡献、促成与投稿。

sensesIntro.en: From putting a share into a common fund, to being one cause of a result, and at last to writing for a shared page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把一份放进公库，到成为一个结果的一项成因，最后到为共同版面写稿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: five hands opening over one jar.
core.cn: 核心意象：五只手在同一只罐子上方张开。

branches.en: The plainest sense puts a share into the pool.
branches.cn: 最朴素的义项是把一份放进公库。

branches.en: A share can also be a cause of what follows.
branches.cn: 一份也可以是后来结果的一项成因。

branches.en: Writing is another way of bringing a dish.
branches.cn: 写稿是端来一道菜的另一种方式。

branches.en: Giving and causing both add something to a whole.
branches.cn: 给予与造成，都是往整体里添东西。

branches.en: A column can also change how readers think.
branches.cn: 一篇专栏也能改变读者的想法。

intro.en: Contribute is built on Latin com-, together, plus tribuere, to allot.
intro.cn: contribute 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tribuere（分配）构成。

latinIntro.en: The allotting base tribut- also appears in contribution, tribute and distribute.
latinIntro.cn: 分配词基 tribut- 也出现在 contribution、tribute 与 distribute 中。

items.meaning: to give a share to a common end
a person who gives a share

definition_zh: 经济的；经济学的；有经济效益的
definition_en: relating to the production, trade and use of money and goods, to economics as a subject, or to something profitable
core_image: 报纸头版全是物价、就业与利率的曲线
scene: 报纸头版全是物价、就业与利率的曲线。 The country entered a long period of economic growth.
sceneCN: 这里 economic 是「经济的」（第 1 个义项：与生产、贸易及金钱有关）；句意为这个国家进入了长期的经济增长期。图中可辨识物件：报纸头版、曲线图、物价数字。

pos.zh: 形容词：经济的；经济学的；有经济效益的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「经济；节约」
由本词加学科后缀构成，义为「经济学」
由本词词干加指人后缀构成，义为「经济学家」
由本词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「节约的；经济实惠的」
由否定前缀与本词构成，义为「不经济的；不划算的」

senses.title: Relating to the economy
senses.titleCN: 经济的：与生产、贸易和金钱有关
senses.definition: relating to the production, distribution and use of goods, money and services in a country or region
senses.definitionCN: 与国家或地区的商品生产、分配、货币及服务有关的
senses.example: The country entered a long period of economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家进入了长期的经济增长期。
senses.why: Greek oikonomia meant managing a household, and the adjective still describes the large-scale version of that management.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 oikonomia 意为「管理家务」，这个形容词描述的仍是这种管理在庞大尺度上的版本。

senses.title: Relating to economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to economics as an academic subject or method of analysis
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学科或分析方法的「经济学」
senses.example: The paper uses an economic model to explain migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文用一个经济学模型解释人口迁移。
senses.why: Once a body of theory grew around household management, the adjective also named the theory rather than the world it studies.
senses.whyCN: 当围绕「家务管理」长出一套理论，这个形容词也用来指理论本身，而不是它所研究的世界。

senses.title: Profitable or viable
senses.titleCN: 有经济效益的：划算、可行
senses.definition: capable of producing enough profit or saving enough money to be worthwhile
senses.definitionCN: 能产生足够利润或省下足够金钱因而值得做的
senses.example: It is not economic to ship the ore by road.
senses.exampleCN: 用公路运矿石并不划算。
senses.why: Management must balance costs and returns, so anything that pays its way can be called economic.
senses.whyCN: 管理必须权衡成本与收益，所以任何能收回成本的东西都可以叫 economic。

intro.en: Economic goes back to a Greek word for running a household, and the modern sense scaled it up to whole nations.
intro.cn: economic 可追到希腊语中「管理家务」的词，现代义把它放大到整个国家。

items.en: Oikos meant house or household, the basic unit of production and consumption.
items.cn: oikos 意为房子、家户，是生产与消费的基本单位。

items.en: Nomos meant law, custom or rule, so oikonomia was the rule of the household.
items.cn: nomos 意为法律、习俗或规则，因此 oikonomia 就是「家户的规则」。

items.en: Oikonomia meant household management and later also the management of public resources.
items.cn: oikonomia 意为家务管理，后来也指公共资源的管理。

items.en: French formed the adjective and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century, when the modern science was taking shape.
items.cn: 法语构成这个形容词，英语在十八世纪借入，正值现代经济学成形之时。

items.en: Economic became the general adjective, while economical specialised in saving money and effort.
items.cn: economic 成为一般形容词，而 economical 专门表示省钱与省力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the economic family and its common confusions; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for money and profitability.
note.cn: 形近组收 economic 词族与常见的混淆词；近义组收表示金钱与盈利的形容词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning thrifty or cheap to run, often confused with economic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的、使用成本低的」，常与 economic 混淆。

entries.definition: The system of money and trade, or the careful use of resources.
entries.definitionCN: 金钱与贸易体系，或对资源的节省使用。

entries.definition: The academic study of production, trade and money.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生产、贸易与金钱的学科。

entries.definition: Relating to money and its management, especially at a personal or corporate level.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱及其管理有关，尤指个人或公司层面。

entries.definition: Relating to trade and business, or intended to make a profit.
entries.definitionCN: 与贸易、商业有关，或目的在于盈利的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a household account book to a national budget and then to the test of whether a plan pays.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一本家用账走到国家预算，再到一项计划是否回本的检验。

normal.en: Economic begins at a kitchen table: oikos is a house, nomos is a rule.
normal.cn: economic 起于一张厨房桌：oikos 是房子，nomos 是规则。

normal.en: Scale the household up and the same word describes a nation's production.
normal.cn: 把家户放大，同一个词就描述一个国家的生产。

normal.en: Economic can also name the theory: an economic model is not the economy.
normal.cn: economic 也可以指理论：an economic model 不是经济本身。

normal.en: If a plan pays for itself, it is economic; if it merely saves, it is economical.
normal.cn: 一项计划若能自己回本，就是 economic；若只是省，就是 economical。

normal.en: Keep economic and financial apart: one is the system, the other is the money in it.
normal.cn: 把 economic 与 financial 分开：一个是系统，一个是系统中的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a single household ledger opened out until it covers a whole country.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家用账簿被摊开，直到覆盖一整个国家。

abstract.en: The same ledger can show wages, prices, taxes or the cost of a new railway.
abstract.cn: 同一本账簿可以显示工资、物价、税收，或一条新铁路的成本。

abstract.en: Economic means the rules by which a society produces and shares what it has.
abstract.cn: economic 意味着一个社会借以生产与分配其所有之物的规则。

examples.en: The country entered a long period of economic growth.
examples.cn: 这个国家进入了长期的经济增长期。

examples.en: The paper uses an economic model to explain migration.
examples.cn: 这篇论文用一个经济学模型解释人口迁移。

examples.en: It is not economic to ship the ore by road.
examples.cn: 用公路运矿石并不划算。

root: 希腊语 oikonomia「家务管理」由 oikos「家户」与 nomos「规则」构成，其形容词经法语 économique 进入英语；现代义扩展到国家经济与经济学。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of economic: the real system of production and trade, the academic study of it, and the practical test of whether something pays.
sensesIntro.cn: economic 的三个义项：真实的生产与贸易体系、对它的学术研究，以及某事物是否回本的实用检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one household ledger is opened out until it covers a whole country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本家用账簿被摊开，直到覆盖一整个国家。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: production, trade and money in a country or region.
branches.cn: 系统线：国家或地区的生产、贸易与金钱。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the theory and models used to study that system.
branches.cn: 学科线：研究该系统的理论与模型。

branches.en: THE TEST: whether a plan produces enough return to be worthwhile.
branches.cn: 检验线：一项计划能否产生足够回报而值得做。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the same household idea appears as a nation and as a model of that nation.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一个「家户」观念，既出现在国家，也出现在国家的模型里。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: costs and returns are weighed whether by a state or by a builder.
branches.cn: 账目线：无论国家还是建造者，都要权衡成本与回报。

intro.en: Economic is a Greek-derived adjective; English adds noun, person and negation affixes around its stem.
intro.cn: economic 是源自希腊语的形容词，英语在其词干周围加名词、指人与否定词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek oikonomia reached English through Latin and French, so the root is Greek while the route is Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 oikonomia 经拉丁语与法语进入英语，因此词根是希腊语，路径是拉丁语。

items.example: The root names the unit being managed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被管理的单位。

items.example: The second root names the rule.
The compound is the direct ancestor of economy.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 economy 的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的
definition_en: carrying a baby inside the body, or full of meaning, feeling or possibility that has not yet shown itself
core_image: 一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部
scene: 候诊室的长椅上，她把手放在小腹上，等护士叫号。 The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
sceneCN: 这里 pregnant 是「怀孕的」（第 1 个义项：体内怀有胎儿）；句意为医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。图中可辨识物件：长椅、候诊室、扶着腹部的手。

pos.zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的

derivatives.zh: 由 pregnant 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「怀孕；孕期」
由前缀 im- 加拉丁词干 pregnant- 构成，义为「使怀孕；使充满」

senses.title: Carrying a child in the body
senses.definition: having a baby or other young growing inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内怀有胎儿或幼崽，正在发育
senses.example: She was pregnant with her second child.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着第二个孩子。
senses.why: Latin praegnans joins prae-, before, with a root for being born, so the word pictures a child who is already there before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praegnans 把表示「在前」的 prae- 与表示出生的词根合在一起，画面是孩子还没降生就已经在那里了。

senses.title: Heavy with meaning that is left unsaid
senses.definition: of a pause, look or remark, so full of meaning that everyone notices what is not said
senses.definitionCN: 指停顿、眼神或话语含义极满，旁人都察觉到没说出口的部分
senses.example: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。
senses.why: A pause that seems to carry something not yet spoken borrows the image of a body holding a hidden life, so the silence looks ready to give birth to a word.
senses.whyCN: 一个仿佛藏着未说之语的停顿，借用了身体怀着一个隐秘生命的画面，于是沉默看上去随时会生出一句话。

senses.title: Full of something about to happen
senses.definition: holding a great deal of a quality or possibility that has not yet come out
senses.definitionCN: 含有大量尚未显现的性质或可能性
senses.example: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。
senses.why: If a body can hold a new life, then anything holding a future can be called pregnant with it, and the preposition with marks what is being carried inside.
senses.whyCN: 身体既然能怀着新生命，任何含着未来的事物也就能说成 pregnant with，介词 with 标出的正是里面所怀的东西。

senses.title: Fertile in invention, of a mind or remark
senses.definition: of a mind or a remark, full of ideas and quick to produce them
senses.definitionCN: 指头脑或言辞充满想法，随时能生出新东西
senses.example: Her pregnant wit turned a dull meeting into a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她机敏的才智把一场沉闷的会议变成了辩论。
senses.why: The oldest figurative use praises a mind that is full and ready to give birth to ideas, a sense now mostly found in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的比喻用法赞美一颗饱满、随时能生出想法的头脑，这层意思如今多见于文学性的文字。

intro.en: Pregnant comes from a Latin adjective that puts before together with a root for birth, and English took it through French with both the bodily and the figurative senses.
intro.cn: pregnant 出自一个把「在前」与「出生」词根合起来的拉丁形容词，英语经法语借入时同时带来了身体义与比喻义。

items.en: The root behind the Latin word for giving birth is usually reconstructed as gen-, meaning to beget; it is a reconstruction, not a word recorded in any text.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语中表示生育的词根可重构为 gen-，意为「生育」；这只是重构形式，并非任何文本里出现过的词。

items.en: Praegnans combined prae-, before, with that root, describing a woman whose child is already there before the birth.
items.cn: praegnans 由表示「在前」的 prae- 与上述词根合成，形容女子在分娩之前就已经怀着孩子。

items.en: The stem pregnant- supplied the cases used in running prose, and it is the shape that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 词干 pregnant- 提供了行文中使用的各个格形式，也正是传入法语、再传入英语的形状。

items.en: Old French used the word for a woman with child and also for a remark heavy with meaning.
items.cn: 古法语既用这个词指怀着孩子的妇人，也用来形容含义沉重的话语。

items.en: English kept both branches, so a woman and a pause can be pregnant, and pregnant with extends the image to anything full of a future.
items.cn: 英语保留了两条分支，于是妇人与停顿都可以是 pregnant，而 pregnant with 把这一意象扩展到任何充满未来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin stem for pregnancy; the near-meaning group gathers words for expecting a child and for meaning held back.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「怀孕」词干上的形式；近义组收表示期待孩子与含义未尽之物的词。

entries.definition: The state or period of carrying a child in the body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pregnant 转成的名词，指怀孕的状态或孕期。

entries.definition: To make someone pregnant, or to fill something through and through.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为使怀孕，或使某物充满。

entries.definition: Relating to the period before birth; it only shares the prefix prae-, and its second element comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 产前的；只是前缀与目标词相近，后半部分来自另一个拉丁词，词源不同。

entries.definition: Waiting for a baby to be born, used of a mother or a family.
entries.definitionCN: 待产的；指母亲或家庭正等待孩子出生。

entries.definition: Carrying eggs or young, the technical word used in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 怀卵的；怀胎的，生物学使用的专业词。

entries.definition: Having a serious or important meaning that is easy to feel.
entries.definitionCN: 有意义的；含有严肃或重要意味的。

entries.definition: Hinting at something without saying it directly.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示的；不直说而让人想到某事的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of carrying a child, and its family keeps returning to hidden life, withheld meaning and stored possibility.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「怀着孩子」的形容词，同族词反复回到隐秘的生命、未尽的意思与储存的可能。

normal.en: Praegnans is prae- plus a birth root, so the word literally places the child before the birth.
normal.cn: praegnans 是 prae- 加表示出生的词根，字面上就是把孩子放在分娩之前。

normal.en: The stem pregnant- carries the meaning through French, and English added no new root of its own.
normal.cn: 词干 pregnant- 把含义一路带到法语，英语没有再添加自己的词根。

normal.en: Pregnant with is the fixed pattern for the figurative sense, as in pregnant with possibility.
normal.cn: pregnant with 是比喻义的固定结构，如 pregnant with possibility。

normal.en: Pregnancy replaces the adjective ending with -cy to name the state rather than the person.
normal.cn: pregnancy 用 -cy 替换形容词词尾，用来指状态而不是人。

normal.en: Impregnate adds im- and shifts the word to the act of filling, whether with a child or with a quality.
normal.cn: impregnate 加 im-，把词义转向「使充满」的动作，充入的可以是孩子，也可以是某种性质。

abstract.en: A pregnant pause and a pregnant woman share one picture: something is inside, alive, and not yet shown.
abstract.cn: 意味深长的停顿与怀孕的妇人共用一幅画面：里面有东西活着，但还没露面。

abstract.en: The word treats the future as something already carried rather than something still to come.
abstract.cn: 这个词把未来当成已经怀在身上的东西，而不是尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: Anything described this way is under pressure to become something else, and that pressure is what the word really names.
abstract.cn: 凡被这样形容的事物，都绷着一股要变成别的东西的力，这个词命名的其实就是这股力。

examples.en: The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
examples.cn: 医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。

examples.en: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
examples.cn: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。

examples.en: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
examples.cn: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个男童」——家里即将扑来一个小男童；pregnant 就是怀孕的。

root: 源自拉丁语 praegnans（怀孕的），由 prae-（在前）与表示出生的词根 gen- 构成，词干 pregnant- 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 pregnancy、impregnate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hidden life carried inside; the senses divide into the bodily state, meaning held back, stored possibility, and an old praise of a fertile mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是怀在里面的隐秘生命；义项由此分出身体状态、未尽的意思、储存的可能，以及对丰沛头脑的旧式赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman resting one hand on her rounded belly and looking down at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部。

branches.en: a hand resting on a rounded belly
branches.cn: 一只手扶着隆起的腹部

branches.en: a speaker stopping mid-sentence while the room waits
branches.cn: 说话人停在半句，满屋等着

branches.en: a seed under soil that has not broken through
branches.cn: 土下尚未破土的种子

branches.en: a notebook crowded with half-finished ideas
branches.cn: 写满未完成想法的笔记本

branches.cn: 一句没说完却暗示更多的话

intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀加上表示出生的词根构成，英语又在同一词干上造出名词与动词。

definition_zh: 改革；革新；改良；改造；改过自新；改革方案
definition_en: to change a system, law, or person's behaviour in order to make it better, or the change itself
core_image: 把一件走形的东西重新浇铸：旧模子被打破，新形状按更好的样子重新定型
scene: 议会大厦里的争论持续了整整一个冬天，新的税收制度终于通过了。 Parliament passed a far-reaching tax reform last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 reform 是「改革方案」（第 6 个义项：作为名词的改革计划）；句意：议会去年春天通过了一项影响深远的税制改革。场景要点：议事厅、表决灯、文件上的条款。

pos.zh: 改革；改良；改造；使改过自新

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「改革；改善；宗教改革运动」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「改革者；改革家」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「主张改革的；改良主义的」
由动词加形容词后缀加名词后缀构成，义为「少年管教所」

senses.title: Change a system for the better
senses.definition: to change a system, organization, or law in order to remove faults and make it work better
senses.definitionCN: 为去除弊端、使其运转更好而改变制度、组织或法律
senses.example: The government promised to reform the pensions system.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承诺改革养老金制度。
senses.why: The Latin formare means 'to shape': reforming is shaping again, giving a faulty thing its form a second time, now with the faults removed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 formare 意为「塑造」：reform 就是「再塑形」，把一件有毛病的东西重新定型，这次去掉毛病。

senses.title: Improve a practice or custom
senses.definition: to make a practice, habit, or method better by changing what is wrong in it
senses.definitionCN: 通过纠正其中的错误来改良某种做法、习惯或方法
senses.example: The club reformed its outdated training routine.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部改良了过时的训练流程。
senses.why: The thing reshaped here is not a law but a way of doing: the new shape replaces the old one piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 这里被重塑的不是法律，而是做事方式：新形状一点一点替换掉旧的。

senses.title: Change a person for the better
senses.definition: to cause someone to give up bad behaviour and live a better life
senses.definitionCN: 使某人改掉坏行为，过上更好的生活
senses.example: The programme claims to reform young offenders through work and study.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目声称通过劳动与学习改造少年犯。
senses.why: A person, like an institution, can be given a new shape: the old habits are broken and better ones are cast in their place.
senses.whyCN: 人和机构一样可以被赋以新形状：旧习惯被打碎，更好的习惯浇铸进原处。

senses.title: Give up bad behaviour oneself
senses.definition: to stop behaving badly and improve one's own way of life, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 指不再作恶、改善自己的生活方式，不带宾语使用
senses.example: After years of trouble he finally reformed and settled down.
senses.exampleCN: 经过多年动荡，他终于改过自新、安顿下来。
senses.why: The shaping verb turns reflexive: the person becomes both the reformer and the thing reformed.
senses.whyCN: 塑造动词转向自身：人既是改革者，又是被重塑之物。

senses.title: Reassemble after breaking up
senses.definition: to come together again or form again after a group or line has been broken up
senses.definitionCN: 指队伍或团体解散后重新集结、重新组成
senses.example: The party reformed three years after it split.
senses.exampleCN: 该党分裂三年后重新组建。
senses.why: The prefix re- does plain work here: form again — the same members take up the old shape, or a nearby one.
senses.whyCN: 这里前缀 re- 只做朴素的工作：再次成形——同一批成员恢复旧的形状，或接近旧的形状。

senses.title: A planned change for the better
senses.definition: a change made to a system, law, or practice in order to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 为改善制度、法律或做法而进行的变革
senses.example: The long-awaited tax reform finally reached Parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 期待已久的税制改革终于提交议会。
senses.why: The noun keeps the whole picture: the old shape, the breaking, and the new shape that replaces it.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了整幅图景：旧形状、打破、以及取而代之的新形状。

senses.title: A person's improvement in character
senses.definition: the fact of a person giving up bad ways and becoming better
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人弃恶从善、变好的事实
senses.example: Everyone noticed his real reform after the months in the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都注意到他在乡下几个月后真正的转变。
senses.why: The reshaped thing is now a life: the noun names the new shape a person has taken on.
senses.whyCN: 此时被重塑的是一段人生：名词命名了一个人呈现出的新形状。

intro.en: Reform comes from Old French reformer, from Latin reformare 'to form again, reshape', from re- 'again' + formare 'to form, shape'. The Latin verb was already used of moral reshaping, and English kept both the institutional and the personal senses.
intro.cn: reform 来自古法语 reformer，上溯拉丁语 reformare「再次成形、重塑」，由 re-「再」加 formare「塑造」构成。拉丁语动词已用于道德重塑，英语同时保留了制度义与个人义。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dher- 'to hold, support, set' underlies Latin forma 'shape, figure', itself of uncertain earlier origin, though often linked to this root.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *dher-「持、撑、置放」是拉丁语 forma「形状」的来源；forma 更早的出处不确定，常被联系到该词根。

items.en: Reformare meant 'to form again, reshape'; Christian writers used it of souls being remade in virtue, so the moral sense is as old as the word.
items.cn: reformare 意为「再次成形、重塑」；教父作家用它指灵魂在德性中被重造，可见道德义与这个词一样古老。

items.en: Old French reformer carried the verb into Romance daily use, covering both reshaping things and reshaping conduct.
items.cn: 古法语 reformer 把该动词带入罗曼语的日常使用，兼指重塑事物与重塑品行。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English around 1300 in the sense 'to convert into a better state'; the personal sense 'to restore from sin' follows in the same century.
items.cn: 动词约在 1300 年已见于英语，义为「使进入更好的状态」；「使人脱离罪恶」的个人义同一世纪出现。

items.en: The noun reform, the political movement sense, and the labels Reformation and reformer establish the word at the centre of public life.
items.cn: 名词 reform、政治运动义，以及 Reformation（宗教改革）与 reformer（改革者）等标签，使这个词坐上公共生活的中心。

note.en: The first group gathers the formare 'shape' family with different prefixes. The second group compares the words for making something better by deliberate change.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 formare「塑造」词族配上不同前缀的词。第二组比较「通过有意的改变使某物变好」的词。

entries.definition: the act of reforming, or the great sixteenth-century religious movement. The noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 改革行为，或十六世纪的宗教改革运动。过程的名词。

entries.definition: a person who works to change a system or a bad habit. It names the shaper, not the shape.
entries.definitionCN: 致力于改变制度或恶习的人。它命名塑造者，而非形状。

entries.definition: literally to shape within, hence to give knowledge or shape to a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 字面是「在内塑形」，引申为赋予知识、启迪心智。

entries.definition: to change the shape completely, across from one kind to another. Transform goes further than reform.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底改变形状，从一种变为另一种。transform 的改变幅度大于 reform。

entries.definition: to shape oneself together with a standard, to fit in.
entries.definitionCN: 使自身与标准同形，即遵从、顺应。

entries.definition: to make better in quality without implying structural change. Improve adds value; reform rebuilds shape.
entries.definitionCN: 在品质上变好，不隐含结构改变。improve 增值；reform 重塑形。

entries.definition: to examine and repair thoroughly, often of machines or systems. Overhaul stresses the full taking-apart.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底检修，多用于机器或制度。overhaul 强调全面拆解。

entries.definition: to correct faults in a text or law, usually by small changes. Amend patches; reform reshapes.
entries.definitionCN: 修正文本或法律中的缺陷，通常是小改动。amend 是打补丁；reform 是重塑。

entries.definition: to organize the parts of a system or company again. It stresses the skeleton rather than the faults.
entries.definitionCN: 重新组织制度或公司的结构。它强调骨架，而非弊端。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'again' + formare 'to shape', the family reformation, reformer, transform and conform, and the picture of casting a new shape.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「再」加 formare「塑造」，词族 reformation、reformer、transform、conform，以及浇铸新形状的图景。

normal.en: re- means again and formare means to shape: reform is giving something a second shape.
normal.cn: re- 是「再」，formare 是「塑造」：reform 就是给某物第二次形状。

normal.en: Form, formal, format and reform all carry the same Latin shape-word.
normal.cn: form、formal、format、reform 都带着同一个拉丁「形状」词。

normal.en: Transform reshapes across kinds; reform reshapes to remove faults; conform reshapes to fit.
normal.cn: transform 跨类重塑；reform 去弊重塑；conform 顺应重塑。

normal.en: Reformation with a capital R names the sixteenth-century religious movement.
normal.cn: 大写 R 的 Reformation 专指十六世纪宗教改革运动。

normal.en: The verb works on laws and on people alike: both can be cast in a new shape.
normal.cn: 这个动词对法律和对人同样有效：两者都能被浇铸成新形状。

abstract.en: Picture a foundry: the old casting is broken up, the metal is melted, and a better shape is poured.
abstract.cn: 想象一间铸造厂：旧铸件被打碎，金属熔化，更好的形状被浇铸出来。

abstract.en: Reform keeps the material and changes the form: nothing new is added, only the shape is replaced.
abstract.cn: reform 保留材质、更换形状：不添加新东西，只是替换形状。

abstract.en: A person who reforms melts down old habits and pours new ones into the same life.
abstract.cn: 改过自新的人熔掉旧习惯，把新的浇进同一段人生。

examples.en: The education ministry began to reform the national curriculum last year.
examples.cn: 教育部去年开始改革国家课程。

examples.en: Many hoped the young offender would reform after serving his sentence.
examples.cn: 许多人希望那个少年犯服刑后能改过自新。

examples.en: Health care reform dominated the whole election campaign.
examples.cn: 医疗改革主导了整场竞选。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福姆」——瑞福把走形的模具「扶」正，重新「模」塑一遍 → reform 改革；改过自新（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 reformare「再次塑造」（re- 再 + formare 塑造），核心是「保留材质、重塑形状以去弊求好」。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of reform, all around one act: shaping again — a system, a practice, or a life is melted down and given a better form.
sensesIntro.cn: reform 的七个义项都围绕同一行为：再次塑造——一个制度、一种做法或一段人生被熔炼，并被赋予更好的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new shape cast over the same material, faults removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：在同一材质上浇出新形状，去掉毛病。

chain: LET THE PERSON HARDEN INTO IT

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND PRACTICES: laws and habits alike are reshaped fault by fault.
branches.cn: 制度与做法：法律与习惯同样被一处一处地重塑。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the shaping turns outward on offenders, or reflexive when a person changes himself.
branches.cn: 人：塑造既可外向作用于犯过者，也可自反——一个人重塑自己。

branches.en: PLAIN RE-FORMING: a broken party or line simply forms again, without any judgement of faults.
branches.cn: 朴素再造：解散的政党或队伍只是再次成形，不涉及任何弊端评判。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the noun names the new shape before it is poured, as a public proposal.
branches.cn: 方案：名词在浇铸之前就命名了新形状，作为公开的提案。

branches.en: THE RESULT: after hardening, the noun names the improved life itself.
branches.cn: 结果：凝固之后，名词命名的是那段变好了的人生本身。

intro.en: Reform carries the Latin prefix re- 'again' on the stem formare 'to shape'. The formare family is one of the widest in English: form, formal, format, inform, transform, conform, deform and perform all share it.
intro.cn: reform 在词干 formare「塑造」上带有拉丁前缀 re-「再」。formare 词族是英语最庞大的词族之一：form、formal、format、inform、transform、conform、deform、perform 都出自它。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is reformare (re- 'again' + formare 'form, shape'), from forma 'shape, figure'. Formare also gives French former and Italian formare with the same meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 reformare（re-「再」+ formare「塑造」），出自 forma「形状」。formare 也生成了法语 former 与意大利语 formare，词义相同。

items.meaning: to shape again; to make better by reshaping
items.meaningCN: 改革；改造（re- 再 + formare 塑造）
items.example: They voted to reform the courts.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票改革司法系统。

items.meaning: the process of reforming; the religious movement
items.meaningCN: 改革；宗教改革运动（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The reformation of the tax code took years.

items.meaningCN: 改革者（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: She is remembered as a great social reformer.
items.exampleCN: 她作为伟大的社会改革家被铭记。

items.meaning: supporting gradual reform rather than revolution
items.meaningCN: 改良主义的（主张渐进改革而非革命）
items.example: The reformist wing won the party vote.
items.exampleCN: 党内改良派赢得了投票。

items.meaning: to shape the mind with facts; to tell
items.meaningCN: 告知；启迪（in- 在内 + formare 塑造）
使彻底改变（trans- 横越 + formare 塑造）
items.exampleCN: 铁路彻底改变了这个地区。

items.meaning: to shape oneself to a standard
items.meaningCN: 遵从；符合（con- 一起 + formare 塑造）
items.example: All products must conform to safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 所有产品必须符合安全规定。

items.meaningCN: 使变形；损毁外形（de- 离去 + formare 塑造）
正式的；形式上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The invitation asked for formal dress.

items.meaning: to carry a task fully into shape; to do
items.meaningCN: 执行；表演（per- 彻底 + formare 塑造）
items.example: The team performed well under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 团队在压力下表现出色。
